classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: poloidal_momentum_flux
items.description: Poloidal momentum flux is the signed transfer rate per unit area of poloidal linear momentum across an oriented surface.
items.documentation:
Poloidal momentum flux describes transport of the poloidal component of [linear momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface. It is the poloidal projection of the [momentum-flux vector](name:momentum_flux) through that surface, including convective, isotropic-pressure, and stress contributions.

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{p}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \left(\mathsf{M}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal momentum flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$ is the vector of momentum transported across the surface per unit area and time, $\mathsf{M}$ is the momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface-normal unit vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal unit vector. The poloidal direction lies in a constant-toroidal-angle plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The population is not fixed: the quantity may describe ions, neutrals, or a total formed by summing the included population contributions. [Poloidal ion momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux) restricts the population to ions. The poloidal label selects the transported momentum component; the transport direction is the surface normal and need not be poloidal or radial. This is a local flux density, not a surface integral or a flux-surface average. Unlike [diamagnetic momentum flux](name:neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_stress), it does not select a diamagnetic contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transferred in the chosen surface-normal direction has a clockwise poloidal component around the magnetic axis, viewed in a poloidal plane with the toroidal symmetry axis on the left.

items.name: thermal_power_of_plant_component_port
items.description: Rate of heat removed from a plant component by coolant, determined by the coolant enthalpy increase between the associated inlet and outlet.
items.documentation:
Thermal power at a plant-component port is the rate of heat energy transferred from the component into the coolant circuit. It is the thermal component of power of a plant component port.

The defining relation is

$$
P_\mathrm{th} = \dot{m}\left(h_\mathrm{out}-h_\mathrm{in}\right)
$$

where $P_\mathrm{th}$ is thermal power, $\dot{m}$ is coolant mass flow rate in kg s$^{-1}$, and $h_\mathrm{in}$ and $h_\mathrm{out}$ are the coolant specific enthalpies at the inlet and outlet in J kg$^{-1}$, respectively.

Positive values mean that the coolant gains enthalpy along the flow path and therefore removes heat from the plant component. This quantity excludes electrical, radiative, and other non-coolant-mediated power transfers.

items.name: floating_electrostatic_potential
items.description: Electrostatic potential of an electrically floating Langmuir-probe collector, relative to a chosen electrical reference, at which the net electric current to the collector vanishes.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the electrostatic potential of an electrically floating Langmuir-probe collector relative to a chosen electrical reference. It is a current-balance-defined value of [electrostatic potential](name:electrostatic_potential), specifying electrostatic interaction energy per positive test charge at the collector.

The defining zero-current condition is

$$
I_{\mathrm{net}}(V_{\mathrm f}) = 0
$$

where $V_{\mathrm f}$ is the floating collector potential relative to the chosen reference and $I_{\mathrm{net}}(V_{\mathrm f})$ is the total signed net electric current to the collector at that potential. Zero net current does not require the individual electron and ion collection currents to vanish.

This quantity applies to the individual collector exposed to the local plasma, without restriction to a wall-mounted collector. It is not a collector-surface average or magnetic-flux-surface mean. The zero-current condition, rather than an externally prescribed bias, defines its value.

The floating collector potential is distinct from the [local plasma potential at a Langmuir-probe position](name:electrostatic_potential_at_langmuir_probe_position). Their difference is governed by sheath current balance and depends on electron temperature and the particle distributions; the two potentials are not interchangeable. The standard deviation of floating-potential fluctuations is a derived fluctuation amplitude, not the signed floating potential itself.

Sign convention: Positive when a positive test charge has greater electrostatic potential energy at the collector than at the chosen reference.

items.name: thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the plasma-volume integral of the local coherent-wave power deposition density into the bulk thermal electron population. It is the thermal-electron component of [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power), rather than the total absorbed power across all plasma channels.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal electron power density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is differential volume.

The integral includes only power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons and excludes deposition into fast electrons, ions, and other channels. Unlike [thermal electron power at inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it covers the complete plasma volume rather than a specified enclosed region.

items.name: ion_charge
items.description: Ion charge number is the net electric charge per ion divided by the positive elementary charge, for a resolved charge state or a specified representative ion population.
items.documentation:
Ion charge number expresses the net electric charge per ion relative to the positive elementary charge. It applies to an identified ionic charge state or a representative charge assigned to a specified ion species or bundled population.

The charge number is defined by:

$$
Z_i = \frac{q_i}{e}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species or population, $Z_i$ is its charge number, $q_i$ is its net electric charge per ion or the corresponding representative charge, and $e$ is the positive elementary charge. This is the ion-specific form of [normalized particle charge](name:normalized_particle_charge) with the elementary charge as its reference.

A resolved charge state has an integer charge number. When a species is represented by its mean charge, the value is the density-weighted mean over all charge states, as defined by [average charge number](name:average_charge_number); a bundled population averages only over its included states. A dominant-state value instead identifies the dominant ionization state and need not equal this mean. Neither a dominant-state selection nor charge-state averaging is implicit in the unqualified quantity.

Unlike [ion atomic number](name:ion_atomic_number), ion charge number depends on the number of bound electrons. It is not the plasma mixture's [effective charge](name:effective_charge), which involves a second charge-number moment over the ion mixture.

[Volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge) spatially averages the relevant local ion charge number over the confined plasma volume. This spatial averaging is distinct from averaging over charge states.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity
items.description: Neutral-internal-state convection velocity is the effective vector velocity that parameterizes nondiffusive advection of the number density of a specified neutral internal state. Its resolved components multiply that state density in the corresponding particle flux.
items.documentation:
Neutral-internal-state convection velocity is the effective vector transport coefficient for nondiffusive advection of particles in a specified neutral internal state. It is scoped to neutral-internal-state particle transport and is not a fully species-independent convection velocity.

The convective particle flux associated with this coefficient is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a = n_a \mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a
$$

where $a$ identifies the specified neutral internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a$ is its convective particle flux, $n_a$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a$ is the neutral-internal-state convection velocity.

This parent quantity denotes the full vector concept; component-resolved quantities such as the [poloidal neutral-internal-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity) are projections of the same neutral-internal-state transport coefficient, not changes of species scope. It excludes diffusive transport coefficients, bulk neutral flow velocity unless that is explicitly the coefficient used in the convective flux relation, and convection velocities for charged-particle species.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a$ points in the positive sense of the component direction named by the resolved standard name.

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
items.description: Toroidal angle of an electron-cyclotron beam is the signed inclination of its mean launch direction out of the local poloidal plane.
items.documentation:
Toroidal angle of electron cyclotron beam

The beam steering angle is defined by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{beam}} = \arcsin\left(\frac{k_\phi}{k}\right)
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{beam}}$ is the toroidal steering angle, $k_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the mean launch wave vector, and $k$ is the magnitude of that mean wave vector. The principal inverse-sine branch is used.

This quantity describes the mean launch direction of one beam, not its spatial toroidal position or the [mechanical rotation angle of a launcher mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror). Together with the [poloidal steering angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), it specifies the mean launch direction. The resulting wave-vector projection along the local magnetic field determines the magnetic-field-parallel refractive index relevant to [electron-cyclotron-driven current](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).

Sign convention: Positive when the mean launch wave vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal azimuth $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: electron_energy_diffusivity
items.description: Electron energy diffusivity is the scalar Fickian coefficient that maps the spatial gradient of electron thermal-energy density to the local diffusive electron thermal-energy flux. It is defined for an electron energy-density-gradient closure, not for a temperature-gradient heat-transport coefficient unless the electron density and heat-capacity factors have been specified.
items.documentation:
Electron energy diffusivity is the scalar local transport coefficient for diffusive smoothing of electron thermal-energy density. It represents only the Fickian, down-gradient part of electron energy transport for the electron population.

The defining closure relates the diffusive electron thermal-energy flux to the gradient of electron thermal-energy density:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,e}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{E,e} \nabla w_e
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,e}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive electron thermal-energy flux, $\chi_{E,e}$ is the electron energy diffusivity, and $w_e$ is the electron thermal-energy density. The minus sign defines the down-gradient convention: positive $\chi_{E,e}$ gives a diffusive flux from larger $w_e$ toward smaller $w_e$.

This quantity excludes convective electron energy transport, explicitly nonlocal transport, and electron energy source or sink terms. It is the electron-population specialization of [energy diffusivity]. It is not equivalent to temperature-gradient electron heat-transport coefficients such as [electron energy diffusion coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient), [parallel electron energy diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity), or [poloidal electron energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity) unless the heat-capacity and density factors relating $\nabla w_e$ to the electron-temperature gradient are part of the definition.

items.name: fast_ion_density
items.description: Number density of fast, nonthermal ions of a specified species, summed over all positive charge states and excluding thermal ions and neutral particles.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{fast}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_i} n_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion number density, $i$ labels the selected ion species, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, $Z_i$ is the species' [atomic number](name:atomic_number), and $n_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its [fast-ion charge-state number density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density) for charge state $q$.

The sum includes all positive charge states of the selected species, not all ion species. Both trapped and passing fast ions are included. Thermal ions and neutral particles are excluded. The quantity counts ions as particles and is distinct from electric charge density and mass density.

It is the fast-population contribution to [ion number density](name:ion_density). When the species population is partitioned into thermal and fast populations, this density plus the corresponding [thermal ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) equals the full number density of that ion species.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position
items.description: Vertical coordinate of a measurement position, specifying its signed location along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate of a measurement position is its signed coordinate along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The [vertical direction] is parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is the projection of the position vector onto the vertical direction:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

Here $Z$ is the vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector from the coordinate origin to the measurement position, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis in the positive vertical direction. In the frame $(R, \phi, Z)$, $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above the positive vertical direction.

This is one coordinate component of the represented measurement position, not the complete position or a measured physical value. Each value pertains to the position under consideration rather than aggregating coordinates over a population of positions. Its corresponding major-radius component is the [radial coordinate of the measurement position](name:radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position).

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the coordinate origin to the measurement position points in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
items.description: Signed rate of vertical momentum gain or loss per unit volume for ions in one specified charge state in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion charge-state momentum source represents local gain or loss of the vertical component of [momentum](name:momentum) per unit volume for a specified ion charge state in the edge plasma. The vertical direction is parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The defining projection is:

$$
S_{s,Z} = \mathbf{S}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the specified ion species and charge state, $\mathbf{S}_s$ is its [momentum source density](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), $S_{s,Z}$ is its vertical component, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing vertical height $Z$. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

The quantity applies locally in the edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer and divertor. Represented source contributions are combined algebraically within the specified charge state; there is no sum over charge states. Unlike the [parallel ion charge-state momentum source](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which projects along the magnetic field, this component follows the symmetry axis.

This is a volumetric source term, not the [vertical ion charge-state momentum flux](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) across a surface. The declared unit has the dimensions of momentum flux rather than volumetric momentum source density and is inconsistent with this definition.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transfer to the specified charge state is directed toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: vertical_angle_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description: Signed elevation angle of the beamlet at the center of a neutral beam injector's injection-unit surface, measured relative to the horizontal plane.
items.documentation:
At the neutral beam injector, this signed elevation angle is the angle of the beamlet at the center of the injection-unit surface relative to the horizontal plane.

The signed elevation angle $\alpha$ is defined by:

$$
\alpha = \arcsin\left(\hat{\mathbf u}\cdot\hat{\mathbf z}\right)
$$

Here, $\alpha$ is the signed elevation angle, $\hat{\mathbf u}$ is the unit vector along the beamlet's propagation axis, and $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is the unit vector in the [vertical direction], parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. The horizontal plane is perpendicular to $\hat{\mathbf z}$. The frame is right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{\mathbf z}$ points toward increasing $Z$.

The value refers specifically to the beamlet at the center of the injection-unit surface; it is not an average over other beamlets or a measure of angular spread, and does not imply that all beamlets share this direction. It specifies vertical pointing rather than toroidal pointing or injector position: the [vertical coordinate of the neutral beam injector](name:vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector) describes position along the same direction, while the [vertical width of the beamlet group](name:vertical_width_of_beamlet_group) describes the group's vertical spatial extent.

Sign convention: Positive when the beamlet propagates with a component toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over directional component forms.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in a specified charge state $z$, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux for that charge state and the local ion temperature gradient. It is the charge-state-resolved specialization of the [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective, advective, and $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized diffusive energy flux is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}\,\nabla T_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their number density, and $T_{i,z}$ is their temperature. The minus sign denotes transport down the local temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over charge states. Its directional realizations include the [radial thermal ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), while the corresponding charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) represents a density-weighted mean over ion species and charge states.

items.name: ion_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient relating aggregate charged-ion transport to ion-number-density gradients, with directional projections represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation:
Ion particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by an ion-number-density gradient. It is the ion-population component of [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional projections represented by quantities such as [radial ion particle diffusivity](name:radial_ion_particle_diffusivity).

For a resolved physical direction $i$, the diffusive ion-particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{ion},i}=-D_{\mathrm{ion},i}\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{ion}}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{ion},i}$ is the ion-particle flux component, $D_{\mathrm{ion},i}$ is the corresponding particle diffusivity component, $n_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the aggregate ion number density, and $x_i$ is the physical coordinate along the resolved transport direction.

The aggregate coefficient describes the total charged-ion population rather than a selected ion charge state. For charge-state aggregation, it is the density-weighted effective diffusivity over the included charged-ion states, not a sum of state-resolved diffusivities.

items.name: nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description: Volumetric nuclear heating power density deposited in breeder-blanket module materials by neutron interactions and associated photon absorption. It is a local material quantity, not a module average or total module heating power.
items.documentation:
Volumetric nuclear heating power density deposited in a breeder blanket module is the local rate of nuclear energy deposition per material volume within the module material. It represents nuclear heating from neutron-induced reactions, recoil and charged-particle products, and associated photon energy absorption in the local material mixture.

The total nuclear heating power of the module is the material-volume integral of the local density:

$$
P_\mathrm{nuc}^{\mathrm{module}} = \int_{V_\mathrm{module}} q_\mathrm{nuc}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_\mathrm{nuc}^{\mathrm{module}}$ is the [nuclear heating power of the breeder blanket module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), $q_\mathrm{nuc}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local nuclear power density at material point $\mathbf{r}$, $V_\mathrm{module}$ is the material volume of the breeder blanket module, and $dV$ is a material-volume element.

This quantity is local to breeder-blanket module material and is not a module-volume average, not the layer-restricted [nuclear power density of a breeder blanket layer](name:nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer), and not the total module nuclear heating power. A layer-specific density restricts the same local physical quantity to an individual functional layer of the module.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from nonthermal particles to bulk thermal electrons, including all source-particle orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from designated nonthermal particle distributions to bulk thermal electrons. It includes all guiding-center orbit classes of the source particles and is a source or sink of electron energy, not stored electron energy.

The transfer is defined by the kinetic-energy moment of the collision operator acting on the thermal electrons:

$$
P_e^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_a \int \varepsilon_e(\mathbf{p})\,C_{ea}[f_e,f_a](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{p})\,d^3p
$$

where $P_e^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-electron collisional power density, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{p}$ is electron momentum, and $\varepsilon_e$ is electron kinetic energy. The function $f_e$ is the thermal-electron momentum distribution, $f_a$ is a designated nonthermal source distribution labeled by $a$, and $C_{ea}$ is the Coulomb-collisional time derivative of $f_e$ caused by interactions with $f_a$. The integral covers all electron momenta; the sum superposes the designated nonthermal source populations.

This is the thermal-target specialization of [electron collisional power density](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions). It excludes energy delivered to nonthermal electrons and energy transfer by noncollisional mechanisms. For energy-conserving binary collisions, the transfer has the opposite sign to the corresponding kinetic-energy change of the nonthermal source particles.

The [co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), and [trapped](name:trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) contributions sum to the orbit-unrestricted transfer when evaluated with the same spatial averaging. These orbit restrictions apply to the nonthermal source particles, not the receiving electrons. The local quantity need not be constant on a magnetic flux surface; a flux-surface-averaged member denotes the average of its corresponding local contribution, and averaging is not intrinsic to this definition.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic energy into the bulk thermal-electron population.

items.name: breakdown_magnetic_field
items.description: Breakdown magnetic-field strength associated with local magnetic induction during plasma initiation, without selecting a particular source contribution or field-strength representation.
items.documentation:
The breakdown magnetic field is the local field-strength characterization of the [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) relevant to plasma initiation and electron-avalanche breakdown. It represents the magnetic environment at the evaluation location without selecting a particular external-coil residual, cylindrical component, or magnitude operation.

The quantity is interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is local to the plasma-initiation setting and carries no implied species, charge-state, spatial integration, or averaging over a region.

This parent is broader than any source-specific or reduction-specific field-strength quantity. It is distinct from the [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), which is a directional cylindrical projection, and from the full magnetic-induction vector represented by [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field).

The [stray breakdown magnetic field](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field) specializes this quantity to the residual field at the plasma position produced by incomplete cancelation of external-coil fields, which can inhibit electron-avalanche breakdown. The related [stray breakdown magnetic field magnitude](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude) further specifies a magnitude representation of that residual field.

items.name: radial_ion_state_energy_flux
items.description: Cylindrical-radial component of the energy-flux density carried by ions in one resolved charge state, signed according to increasing major radius.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the radial projection of the energy-flux density associated with one specified ion charge state. It retains the net signed energy transport of that state and is the radial component of [ion state energy flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux).

$$
\mathcal{F}_{i,q,R}=\boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}_{i,q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}_{i,q}$ is the energy-flux-density vector for ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, $\mathcal{F}_{i,q,R}$ is its radial component in W m$^{-2}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector of increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The quantity is resolved by charge state and is not summed over other ionization states. For a noncircular magnetic flux surface, this cylindrical-radial projection is distinct from a flux-surface-normal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated energy-flux vector has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_temperature
items.description: Temperature of a specified ion species from random translational motion, arithmetically averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Temperature of a specified ion species averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of its local kinetic temperature. The local temperature represents the isotropic part of random translational energy and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The volume average of the local [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature) is defined by

$$
\langle T_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_i\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_i\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged temperature of the specified ion species, $T_i$ is its local temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the differential physical-volume element.

For the specified species, the local temperature is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states; [ion charge-state temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature) resolves an individual charge state. The subsequent spatial average is an arithmetic volume average, not a density-weighted particle average or a volume-integrated thermal energy. It does not combine different ion species, unlike [ion average temperature](name:ion_average_temperature).

[Volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature) is the corresponding electron-population quantity. This ion-species volume average supplies the denominator in the [ratio of magnetic-axis ion temperature to volume-averaged ion temperature](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature), which expresses central temperature peaking.

items.name: trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source per plasma volume delivered to trapped fast ions in a specified charge state through Coulomb collisions.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated with Coulomb momentum transfer to trapped fast ions in a specified charge state. The trapped orbit class selects the contribution from that population, while directional components select projections without changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the rotation axis, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to the trapped fast-ion charge-state population, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the corresponding unit vector.

This is the trapped-orbit realization of [fast ion charge state torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It retains the full angular-momentum-transfer vector; [toroidal trapped fast ion charge state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) selects its toroidal component, while [co-passing fast ion charge state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) selects another orbit class.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description: Mean translational velocity of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state, projected along the toroidal symmetry axis in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the vertical component of the local [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) in the edge plasma. It describes directed motion of a neutral species in one specified quantum or energy state along the toroidal symmetry axis.

The component is the normalized first velocity moment projected onto the vertical direction:

$$
u_{0,a,Z}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{0,a}(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{0,a,Z}$ is the vertical bulk velocity component, $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is the corresponding bulk velocity vector, subscript $0$ denotes neutrals, and $a$ identifies the specified internal state. Here $\mathbf r$ is spatial position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_{0,a}$ is the phase-space number density of the selected neutral species and state. The integrals extend over all particle velocities. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf z}$ points along increasing vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The averaging is within the specified species and internal state; different internal states and other species are not combined. The velocity is defined where the selected state's number density is nonzero. Bulk denotes mean translational flow, not an additional hot- or cold-population restriction. This component is neither the flow-speed magnitude, a thermal velocity spread, nor a particle flux.

The [radial neutral internal-state velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity) is the distinct major-radius projection of the state-resolved flow; the vertical component instead follows the symmetry-axis direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral internal-state bulk flow has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: gap_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Minimum geometric clearance between the plasma separatrix and the nearest limiter or wall element.
items.documentation:
The plasma-boundary gap is the shortest Euclidean separation between the last closed magnetic-flux surface, or separatrix, and any limiter or wall element. It characterizes the closest plasma-facing boundary clearance.

The gap is defined by

$$
d_{\mathrm{gap}}=\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{sep}},\,\mathbf{y}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{pw}}}\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2
$$

where $d_{\mathrm{gap}}$ is the plasma-boundary gap, $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on the separatrix $\Gamma_{\mathrm{sep}}$, $\mathbf{y}$ is a point on the combined limiter-or-wall boundary $\Gamma_{\mathrm{pw}}$, and $\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|_2$ is their Euclidean distance.

The quantity applies to the plasma separatrix and the nearest eligible limiter or wall element, with aggregation by the minimum over all eligible boundary-point pairs. The geometric points are interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is a shortest geometric clearance, not a radial coordinate, a distance to an arbitrarily selected wall point, or an average over the wall. The separatrix is the boundary identified by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the plasma boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary); the gap then measures its closest separation from plasma-facing material.

items.name: poloidal_current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux
items.description: Poloidal magnetic flux from all external active coils and passive loops is averaged over the plasma cross-section with toroidal-current-density weighting, excluding plasma-generated flux.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux from external circuits, averaged with toroidal-current-density weighting over the plasma poloidal cross-section, represents the externally generated flux linked by the plasma current. It specializes [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) by selecting the external poloidal contribution and its current-weighted average.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height, the average is defined by

$$
\overline{\Phi}_{\mathrm{p,ext}} = \frac{\displaystyle\int_{\Omega_p} \Phi_{\mathrm{p,ext}}(R,Z)\,j_\phi(R,Z)\,dA}{I_p}
$$

where $\overline{\Phi}_{\mathrm{p,ext}}$ is the current-weighted average external poloidal magnetic flux, $\Omega_p$ is the plasma poloidal cross-section, $dA$ is its area element, and $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the plasma [current density](name:current_density). The signed total toroidal plasma current is $I_p=\int_{\Omega_p}j_\phi\,dA$. The local external poloidal flux $\Phi_{\mathrm{p,ext}}$ is the signed flux of externally generated magnetic field through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle through the evaluation point.

The external contribution includes all active coils and passive conducting loops, including induced currents; their flux contributions are summed before averaging. Flux generated by the plasma current itself is excluded, as in [external magnetic flux](name:external_magnetic_flux). This quantity is the poloidal specialization of [current-weighted average external magnetic flux](name:current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux), not an unweighted area average or a flux evaluated at a single location. The normalization requires nonzero total plasma current and uses signed current density rather than its absolute value.

Sign convention: Positive when the external flux through the horizontal disks, averaged with the signed weights $j_\phi/I_p$, is directed toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: safety_factor_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Safety factor at the magnetic axis is the limiting signed number of toroidal field-line turns per poloidal circuit as neighboring closed flux surfaces approach the axis.
items.documentation:
Safety factor at magnetic axis

In axisymmetry, or using straight-field-line flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, the neighboring-surface [safety factor](name:safety_factor) is defined by

$$
q = \frac{1}{2\pi}\oint \frac{\mathbf{B}\cdot\nabla\phi}{\mathbf{B}\cdot\nabla\theta}\,d\theta
$$

where $q$ is the signed safety factor, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, $\rho$ is a monotonic flux-surface label vanishing at the magnetic axis, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The integral covers one complete poloidal circuit. The toroidal angle belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height; increasing $\phi$ is counterclockwise when viewed from above.

The axis value $q_0$ is defined by the limit $q_0 = \lim_{\rho\to0}q(\rho)$, rather than by direct evaluation of the poloidal-angle integral at the axis. It is a locus-specific value, not a spatial average or a sum. It is also distinct from the [minimum safety factor](name:minimum_safety_factor), which selects the signed value where the winding magnitude is smallest and need not occur at the magnetic axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angle advance of a magnetic field line is in the direction of increasing $\phi$ as the poloidal angle $\theta$ increases.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: ion_charge_number
items.description: The ionic charge number assigned to one ion species, given by a number-density-weighted mean over all charge states when the distribution is explicit, or by the represented dominant-state or effective charge number otherwise.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the ionic charge number assigned to one ion species. For an explicitly represented charge-state distribution, it is the number-density-weighted mean ionic charge number; a dominant-state representation gives the charge number of that state, while a lumped isonuclear sequence may be represented by an effective charge number.

For an explicitly represented distribution, the species mean is defined by:

$$
\overline{Z}_i = \frac{\sum_q q\,n_{i,q}}{\sum_q n_{i,q}}
$$

Here $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is the integer ionic charge number of a charge state, and $n_{i,q}$ is the [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) of species $i$ in state $q$; $\overline{Z}_i$ is the resulting species charge number.

The aggregation is the density-weighted mean over all charge states of this one species. It is not an unweighted average or a sum across distinct ion species; a value restricted to a specified charge-state bundle is [ion charge-state charge number](name:ion_charge_state_charge_number).

For an explicit charge-state distribution, this is the species-specific [average charge number](name:average_charge_number).

items.name: radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Radial cross-field diffusion coefficient for thermal energy carried by the total ion population, summed over all ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
The radial ion energy diffusion coefficient is the Fick's-law proportionality coefficient for cross-field transport of thermal energy carried by the total ion population. It aggregates all ion species and charge states.

The radial diffusive thermal-energy flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,E,r}\frac{\partial w_{i,E}}{\partial r}
$$

where $D_{i,E,r}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $\Gamma_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive thermal-energy flux density, $w_{i,E}$ is the total ion thermal-energy density, and $r$ is the radial transport coordinate. The minus sign denotes transport down the thermal-energy-density gradient.

This quantity is the radial component of [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), not the energy flux itself. It differs from the charge-state-resolved [radial thermal ion charge state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and excludes electron thermal-energy transport, described by the [radial electron energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: radial_electron_convection_velocity
items.description: Signed major-radius component of the effective velocity multiplying electron number density in the convective electron particle flux, excluding density-gradient-driven diffusion.
items.documentation:
Radial electron convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the density-proportional convective electron particle flux along the major-radius direction. It describes directed electron transport after density-gradient-driven diffusion has been separated.

The radial convective electron particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_e v_{e,R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the major-radius component of the convective electron particle flux, $n_e$ is electron number density, and $v_{e,R}$ is this radial convection velocity.

The quantity applies to electron particle transport, not ion or neutral particle transport, and is not summed over those populations. Its direction is the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This direction is not generally normal to magnetic flux surfaces.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and need not equal the bulk electron flow velocity. It is the radial component of [electron convection velocity]; the explicitly particle-channel [electron particle convection velocity](name:electron_particle_convection_velocity) denotes the corresponding unprojected vector. It is a particle-transport coefficient, not a heat- or momentum-transport coefficient.

Sign convention: Positive when electron convection points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
items.description: Neutral internal-state energy flux is the signed thermal energy transported per unit area and time across an oriented surface by one neutral species in one specified internal state.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state energy flux is the net thermal-energy transport across an oriented surface per unit area and time, carried by neutral particles of one species in one specified internal state. It includes the total thermal-energy transport contribution, rather than only its diffusive part.

The oriented-surface flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{W,0,a}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,0,a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,0,a}$ is the signed surface-normal energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,0,a}$ is the thermal-energy-flux vector of the selected neutral population, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen unit normal to the surface. The subscripts $W$, $0$, and $a$ identify the thermal-energy channel, neutral particles, and the specified internal state, respectively.

This quantity applies to one neutral species and one internal state; it is not summed over states or species. It is an energy flux density, not a particle-number flux or a surface-integrated power. Summing the state-resolved energy-flux vectors over all internal states of the same species gives the [neutral species energy flux](name:neutral_species_energy_flux), using the same thermal-energy convention.

The [parallel neutral internal-state energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) and [poloidal neutral internal-state energy flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) are directional specializations, selecting the local magnetic-field and poloidal directions, respectively. No particular projection direction is imposed by this general definition.

Sign convention: Positive when net thermal energy carried by the selected neutral state crosses the surface in the direction of its chosen unit normal.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fickian coefficient relating major-radius-directed diffusive particle flux to the opposing number-density gradient for ions of one species and charge state.
items.documentation:
The radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient characterizes particle diffusion of one specified ion species and charge state along the major-radius direction. It is the radial-radial diagonal component of the particle-diffusion tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the response to the major-radius density gradient alone, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{R}^{s,q,\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{RR}^{s,q}\frac{\partial n_{s,q}}{\partial R}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is its ionic charge number, $\Gamma_{R}^{s,q,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the major-radius-directed diffusive particle-flux contribution driven by that gradient, $D_{RR}^{s,q}$ is this diffusion coefficient, and $n_{s,q}$ is the number density of the selected species and charge state. The derivative is taken at fixed $\phi$ and $Z$. The minus sign makes positive diffusivity correspond to down-gradient particle transport.

The density and flux include thermal and nonthermal particles of the selected charge state, without summing over charge states or ion species. This coefficient describes particle transport, not energy diffusion, and does not include convective flux or off-diagonal diffusion-tensor responses. The major-radius direction is not generally normal to magnetic flux surfaces or perpendicular to the magnetic field.

This is the major-radius directional specialization of the [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient). In contrast, the [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) relates charge-state-summed particle flux to the charge-state-summed density gradient without selecting a spatial direction.

items.name: neutral_particle_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective velocity multiplying particle density in the density-proportional convective part of particle transport, independent of particle species and directional component.
items.documentation:
The particle convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the density-proportional, convective contribution to particle transport. It represents directed drift, pinch, or outward convection after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has been separated, and it is the shared quantity represented by particle convection velocity.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n\,\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle-flux vector, $n$ is particle number density, and $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the particle convection-velocity vector.

This parent quantity is independent of species and directional component; specific children may resolve it for a selected population or component, as in [parallel neutral particle convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity). It excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport.

Sign convention: Positive when a reported component of convective particle transport points along its positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis, or along the specified magnetic-field direction for a parallel component.

items.name: neutron_rate_of_neutron_detector
items.description: Neutron rate of a neutron detector is the rate of accepted neutron-induced detection events registered by the detector, distinct from incident neutron flux, detector efficiency, and total neutron source emission.
items.documentation:
Neutron rate of a neutron detector is the time rate of individually accepted neutron-induced detection events registered by that detector.

It is defined from the cumulative accepted neutron-event count:

$$
R_n(t) = \frac{dN_\mathrm{det}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $R_n(t)$ is the neutron detection rate and $N_\mathrm{det}(t)$ is the cumulative number of accepted neutron-induced detector events up to time $t$.

This quantity is a detector response count rate. It excludes non-neutron events and is distinct from the incident [neutron flux of a neutron detector](name:neutron_flux_of_neutron_detector), the [efficiency of a neutron detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_neutron_detector), and the total neutron emission rate of the source.

items.name: rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping
items.description: Global particle-number throughput removed from the plasma by pumping at the wall, independent of any particular carrier species and distinct from an areal flux.
items.documentation:
The wall-attributed pumping rate is the global particle-number throughput removed from the plasma through the wall by a pumping process. It applies to the aggregate removed particle population without selecting a particular species or charge state.

The rate is defined as

$$
R_{\rm pump} = \frac{dN_{\rm removed}}{dt}
$$

where $R_{\rm pump}$ is the pumping-related particle-removal rate, $N_{\rm removed}$ is the cumulative number of particles removed through the wall, and $t$ is time.

This quantity is a global throughput rather than a local particle flux per unit wall area; spatially resolved wall fluxes must be integrated over the relevant wall surface before forming this rate. It excludes particle removal mechanisms not attributed to pumping. The quantity is the wall-localized specialization of [rate due to pumping](name:rate_due_to_pumping), while [particle rate at wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping) makes the particle-channel interpretation explicit without restricting the carrier species.

items.name: accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of carbon-13-labeled methane delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, with ten count units assigned to each neutral 13CH4 molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral carbon-13-labeled methane introduced by gas injection after plasma breakdown. It counts injected molecules rather than free electrons retained in the plasma.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=10\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}(t')\,dt'
$$

Here $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the injection rate of neutral methane molecules in s$^{-1}$, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, $t$, and $t'$ are times in seconds. The factor 10 is the sum of six equivalent electrons from carbon and four from hydrogen in each neutral molecule; carbon-13 labeling does not change the atomic number. The quantity excludes methane introduced during prefill, which is represented by [methane carbon-13 prefill count](name:methane_carbon_13_prefill_count), and is the time integral of the corresponding [methane carbon-13 source rate](name:methane_carbon_13_source_rate).

items.name: parallel_ion_particle_flux
items.description: Parallel ion particle flux is the signed net flow of one specified ion species along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion particle flux is the signed net flow of one specified ion species along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time, summed over its ionic charge states.

The field-parallel flux is the projection of the ion particle-flux vector and the sum of its charge-state contributions:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf b} = \sum_c \Gamma_{ic,\parallel}
$$

Here, $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel particle flux of species $i$, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is that species' local particle-flux vector, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. The index $c$ labels an ionic charge state, and $\Gamma_{ic,\parallel}$ is the [parallel ion charge-state particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for species $i$ in charge state $c$.

The quantity applies to one specified ion species and is summed over all its ionic charge states, counting each ion particle once rather than weighting by charge. It does not combine distinct ion species and excludes neutral particles. It is a local flux density referred to area perpendicular to the magnetic field, not a surface-integrated particle rate or a one-way incident flux.

This is the field-parallel component of the [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux); its charge-state contributions add algebraically, so oppositely directed flows can cancel. It describes particle-number transport, not electric-current density or energy flux.

Sign convention: Positive when the net ion flow is directed along the local magnetic field.

items.name: total_ion_power_density
items.description: Total ion power density is the net local energy-transfer rate to the ion channel, aggregated over all included ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Total ion power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from all included ion species per unit volume. It is the aggregate source term for the ion recipient in an ion energy transport equation, summed over ion charge states and included ion-channel contributions.

For a differential volume, the aggregate ion-channel source term is defined by

$$
S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{total}} = \sum_c \sum_s \sum_Z S_{E,c,s,Z} = \frac{\partial^2 E_i^{\mathrm{total}}}{\partial t\,\partial V}
$$

where $S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{total}}$ is total ion power density, $c$ indexes included ion-energy channels, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ indexes charge states, $E_i^{\mathrm{total}}$ is energy transferred to the ion population in joules, $t$ is time in seconds, and $V$ is physical volume in cubic meters. It is the aggregate form of [ion power density](name:ion_power_density), including contributions such as [thermal ion power density](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density) and fast-ion power density when those channels belong to the same balance. Spatial redistribution by the divergence of ion energy flux is excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when the aggregate ion population gains energy in the ion energy transport equation.

items.name: poloidal_electron_particle_flux
items.description: Poloidal electron particle flux is the signed net electron crossing rate per unit area perpendicular to the local direction around a plasma cross-section.
items.documentation:
Poloidal electron particle flux is the local signed number flow of free electrons along the poloidal direction per unit area perpendicular to that direction. Opposite crossing directions contribute with opposite signs.

The poloidal component is defined by the projection

$$
\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electron particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the electron number-transport vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{p}}$ is the oriented local poloidal unit tangent. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The poloidal tangent lies in a plane of constant $\phi$, with its orientation set by the specified poloidal-angle convention rather than by the magnetic-field direction.

In edge-plasma transport, this quantity describes local electron number transport around the plasma cross-section. It is neither a surface-integrated rate nor a poloidal average, and its direction is not generally magnetic-field-parallel or flux-surface-normal.

It specializes [electron particle flux](name:electron_particle_flux) to a surface normal to the local poloidal direction. It counts electrons without electric-charge or energy weighting, unlike [poloidal electron energy flux](name:poloidal_electron_energy_flux), which describes their kinetic-energy transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the net electron number flow follows the specified positive poloidal tangent around the plasma cross-section.

items.name: electron_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective electron particle diffusivity relating diffusive number flux to the opposing number-density gradient, without selecting a spatial direction.
items.documentation:
The electron diffusion coefficient characterizes electron particle transport driven by the local electron number-density gradient. It specifies a Fickian diffusive response without prescribing a spatial direction or restricting the quantity to a particular plasma region.

For an uncoupled directional response along a unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$, the defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_u = -D^e_u\,\hat{\mathbf{u}}\cdot\nabla n_e
$$

where $\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_u$ is the diffusive electron particle flux density projected along $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$, $D^e_u$ is the electron diffusion coefficient for that directional response, $n_e$ is the electron number density, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The subscript $u$ labels the selected direction, and the superscript $e$ denotes electrons. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for positive diffusivity.

This is a particle-transport coefficient, distinct from electron energy diffusivity, and excludes convective contributions to electron particle flux. No isotropy is implied: the [poloidal electron diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient) is its poloidal-poloidal diagonal specialization in an anisotropic diffusion tensor. The coefficient alone does not specify off-diagonal tensor couplings.

items.name: straight_field_line_angle
items.description: An angular coordinate that labels position along magnetic field lines after a straight-field-line transformation, making field-line trajectories linear on each magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
A straight-field-line angle is an angular coordinate for labeling position along magnetic field lines in a magnetic-flux coordinate description. The transformation is chosen so that field-line trajectories are straight, or have constant angular slope, on each flux surface.

This quantity denotes the coordinate itself rather than a mechanical steering angle, wave phase, or physical distance along a field line. Its origin, angular orientation, and selected angular direction are defined by the associated straight-field-line coordinate convention.

The [poloidal straight-field-line angle] is the poloidal specialization of this general coordinate concept. Other specializations, when defined, differ by the angular direction or coordinate convention rather than by a different underlying physical quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when position advances in the defined positive direction of the straight-field-line angular coordinate.

items.name: net_power_of_plant_system
items.description: Net real electrical power of a plant system, defined as generation minus internal electrical consumption at the same system boundary; positive values denote net export.
items.documentation:
Net power of a plant system is the real electrical power balance of one plant system, with generation counted positively and internal consumption counted negatively. It is the generated-minus-consumed counterpart to the load-oriented [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system), rather than thermal, apparent, reactive, or accumulated energy.

For a consistently defined system boundary, the net power is defined as

$$
P_\mathrm{net} = P_\mathrm{generated} - P_\mathrm{consumed} = -P_\mathrm{system}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{net}$ is this plant-system quantity, $P_\mathrm{generated}$ is real electrical power generated within the boundary, $P_\mathrm{consumed}$ is real electrical power consumed within the boundary, and $P_\mathrm{system}$ is [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) using the load-positive convention. Internal transfers between included subsystems cancel. The quantity is the negative of net absorbed power of a plant system when both use the same boundary and scope; positive values denote net electrical export from the system boundary.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_density
items.description: Number density of neutral particles of a specified species in one internal quantum state, including both thermal and nonthermal populations.
items.documentation:
Number density of neutral

At a given position and time, the density is the zeroth velocity moment of the state-resolved distribution:

$$
n_{s,a}^{0} = \int f_{s,a}^{0}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,a}^{0}$ is the neutral number density, $s$ identifies the species, $a$ identifies its internal quantum state, and the superscript $0$ denotes electrical neutrality. The function $f_{s,a}^{0}$ is the velocity distribution of those neutral particles, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all velocities.

The quantity retains the specified internal state rather than summing over internal states. Ionized particles and neutral particles in other internal states are excluded; thermal and nonthermal particles in the selected state are both included.

For the same species and internal state, this density is the sum of the [thermal contribution](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density) and the [fast nonthermal contribution](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density). Summing it over all internal states gives the [neutral-species density](name:neutral_species_density) of that species.

items.name: heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Positive e-folding distance for the outward decrease of heat-flux magnitude across magnetic flux surfaces in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the positive cross-field decay length of heat-flux magnitude in the scrape-off layer. It is the heat-flux specialization of [decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

For an outward-decreasing heat flux, the defining relation is

$$
\lambda_q = \left|\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $\lambda_q$ is the heat-flux decay length, $q$ is the positive heat-flux magnitude of the specified heat channel, and $x$ is outward physical distance across magnetic flux surfaces at the reference location. For exponential falloff, this scale is constant; otherwise it describes the local logarithmic decrease.

The heat channel is not fixed by this parent quantity, and no particular species sum is implied. The [electron heat decay length](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) and [ion heat decay length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) are its species-resolved specializations.

The divertor-entrance form uses the heat-flux distribution mapped to the outboard midplane, with $x$ and $\lambda_q$ expressed as outboard-midplane distances. In this form, $\lambda_q$ is the upstream exponential decay parameter, distinct from the spreading length $S$, which describes additional broadening of the divertor-target heat-flux distribution. It is not the full width of the broadened target footprint, a density decay length, or a temperature decay length.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_constraint_position
items.description: Poloidal magnetic flux at the constraint position is the signed equilibrium flux through a horizontal disk bounded by the toroidal circle passing through that position.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the constraint position is the signed flux through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle through that position. It is a location-specific poloidal specialization of [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux), labeling the magnetic surface through that position in axisymmetric equilibrium.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height increasing upward, the defining relation is evaluated at the constraint position:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}(R,Z) = 2\pi \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, and $R'$ is the integration variable for major radius.

This value includes both externally generated and plasma-generated magnetic-field contributions; it is neither a spatial average nor an external-source-only flux. It differs from [toroidal magnetic flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux), which threads a poloidal cross-section rather than a horizontal disk.

Evaluating the same flux function on the plasma boundary gives the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). For nested magnetic surfaces with toroidal plasma current flowing toward increasing $\phi$, the poloidal flux decreases from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic field threading the horizontal integration disk is directed toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Toroidal directional diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of bulk-ion momentum as the toroidal diagonal component of the ion momentum diffusivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient is the toroidal directional component of the [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) vector and the $\hat{\phi}\hat{\phi}$ diagonal component of the bulk-ion momentum diffusivity tensor. It relates the diffusive flux of charge-state-summed bulk-ion toroidal momentum density along $\hat{\phi}$ to the local gradient of that momentum density along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a gradient-diffusion closure, this diagonal component satisfies:

$$
\Pi_{\phi\phi,i}^{\rm diff} = -\chi_{\phi,i}\,\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial}{\partial \phi}\left(m_i n_i v_{\phi,i}\right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi\phi,i}^{\rm diff}$ is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection of the diffusive flux of bulk-ion toroidal momentum density, positive for transport in the direction of increasing $\phi$; $\chi_{\phi,i}$ is this coefficient; $m_i$ is ion mass; $n_i$ is bulk-ion number density summed over all charge states; and $v_{\phi,i}$ is the density-weighted mean bulk-ion flow velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$ over all charge states, positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$. The derivative is taken at fixed $R$ and $Z$, so $R^{-1}\partial/\partial\phi$ is the directional derivative along $\hat{\phi}$.

The toroidal qualifier denotes the tensor direction of both the transported momentum component and the spatial flux-gradient projection; it is not a cross-flux-surface coefficient for transport of toroidal momentum. This distinguishes it from [toroidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which is charge-state resolved and flux-surface-normal, positive toward increasing flux label. Convective momentum transport, explicit momentum sources or sinks, and residual-stress contributions are excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when a positive derivative of the bulk-ion toroidal momentum density along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ produces a diffusive flux of that momentum in the direction of decreasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description: Effective velocity associated with convective plasma-energy transport, relating the convective energy flux to the energy content being transported.
items.documentation:
Energy convection velocity is the effective transport velocity assigned to the convective part of an energy flux. It characterizes motion of transported energy rather than necessarily the bulk velocity of any individual plasma population.

The effective velocity is defined from the convective energy flux and the corresponding transported energy density:

$$
v_{E,\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{F_{E,\mathrm{conv}}}{\mathcal{E}}
$$

where $v_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the energy convection velocity, $F_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy flux in the relevant transport direction, and $\mathcal{E}$ is the associated transported energy density.

The quantity represents convective transport only and excludes energy transport attributed to diffusion, conduction, radiation, or other separately identified processes. A population- and charge-state-resolved instance is [thermal ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection); it should not be assumed identical to the particle convection velocity or to [ion heat convection velocity](name:ion_heat_convection_velocity) without an explicit energy-transport definition.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
items.description: Poloidal angle of the electron-cyclotron beam's mean propagation direction, measured from inward horizontal toward downward.
items.documentation:
Poloidal angle of electron cyclotron beam

For the beam mean wave vector, the steering angle is defined by

$$\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(Z_{\mathrm{axis}} - Z,\; R - R_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

where $\theta$ is this beam direction angle, $k_R$ is the [radial wave-vector component], and $k_Z$ is the [vertical wave-vector component](name:vertical_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam), with components taken along the $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ directions. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ returns the quadrant-resolved angle for the ordered pair $(x,y)$.

The quantity applies to one electron-cyclotron beam's mean wave vector at the location where its angle is defined; it is not an aggregate across beams or an average of individual ray angles. Unlike [poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam](name:poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam), it describes propagation direction rather than the angular position of trajectory points. Its reference direction is inward, rather than the magnetic-axis-referenced position angle described by [poloidal angle]. Poloidal steering contributes to the radial deposition location but is not itself a deposition-position coordinate.

It complements the [toroidal angle of the electron-cyclotron beam](name:toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), which describes the toroidal component of the beam steering direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the projected mean propagation direction is rotated from inward $-\hat{R}$ toward downward $-\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the relative angular offset of a coherent radio-frequency excitation at a selected strap or module from a specified reference.
items.documentation:
Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna describes the relative phase of a coherent radio-frequency excitation at a selected strap or module. It encompasses feed-voltage phase and inter-element excitation phasing without restricting the excitation to a forward traveling wave or fixing the reference to the first element.

The relative phase is defined by

$$
\varphi_{kr} = \arg\!\left(A_k A_r^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\varphi_{kr}$ is the wave phase of selected element $k$ relative to reference $r$, $A_k$ is the selected excitation phasor, $A_r$ is the coherent reference phasor, the superscript $*$ denotes complex conjugation, and $\arg$ extracts the complex argument. Phasors use the temporal factor $e^{+\mathrm{i}\omega t}$, where $\mathrm{i}$ is the imaginary unit, $\omega$ is their common angular frequency, and $t$ is time. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ and is undefined if either phasor vanishes.

The quantity applies to one specified excitation-reference pair, not a sum or average over antenna elements. For inter-element phasing, the phasors represent the same excitation type at specified reference planes. Relative strap phases shape the launched wave spectrum, but this quantity contains neither excitation amplitude nor power.

The [forward-wave phase](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) specializes this quantity to forward power-wave phasors referenced to the first module. By contrast, the [reflected phase](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) compares reflected and forward waves at the same element rather than excitations at different elements.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected excitation leads its specified reference in phase under the stated temporal convention.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point
items.description: Signed vertical Z coordinate of the first-wall point with minimum geometric distance to the plasma boundary or separatrix in the right-handed cylindrical frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the vertical position of the first-wall location closest to the plasma boundary or separatrix. It identifies a wall point geometrically, rather than a point on the boundary itself or the [vertical coordinate of the plasma boundary](name:vertical_outline_of_plasma_boundary).

$$
\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{fw}}=\underset{\mathbf{p}\in\mathcal{W}}{\operatorname{arg\,min}}\,d(\mathbf{p},\mathcal{B}),\qquad Z_{\mathrm{fw}}=Z(\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{fw}})
$$

Here, $\mathcal{W}$ is the first-wall surface, $\mathcal{B}$ is the relevant plasma boundary or separatrix, $d$ is geometric distance, and $Z$ is vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. The quantity is distinct from [gap at plasma boundary](name:gap_at_plasma_boundary), which gives the corresponding minimum separation rather than its vertical location.

Sign convention: Positive when the closest first-wall point lies in the $+Z$ direction, above the machine midplane.

items.name: poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective particle diffusivity relating an ion species’ poloidal diffusive flux to its opposing poloidal number-density gradient, with density and flux summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
