The poloidal ion diffusion coefficient is the effective ion particle diffusivity along the poloidal tangent on a magnetic flux surface. In flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. It specifies the poloidal-poloidal diagonal response of the particle-transport tensor.

For the diagonal Fickian contribution to the poloidal particle flux:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,\mathrm{pp}}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}\cdot\nabla n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive poloidal particle flux density of the specified ion species, $D_{i,\mathrm{pp}}$ is its poloidal ion diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit tangent toward increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$, $n_i$ is the species’ ion number density, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for positive diffusivity.

Both density and particle flux are summed over all ionic charge states of one specified ion species, excluding neutral particles and other ion species. The coefficient is an effective closure for these totals, not a sum of charge-state diffusion coefficients. The [poloidal ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) instead applies to one specified charge state.

This quantity is the poloidal directional specialization of the [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient), which does not select a spatial direction. It describes particle diffusion rather than energy or momentum diffusion, excludes convective flux and off-diagonal tensor contributions, and does not prescribe a particular transport mechanism.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
items.description: Poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux is the signed net number flow of one neutral species in a specified internal quantum state per unit area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux is the local number transport of one neutral atomic or molecular species in a specified internal quantum state along the poloidal direction. Opposite crossing directions contribute with opposite signs.

The defining projection is

$$
\Gamma_{0,a,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}} = \int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}})f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,a,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a}$ is the particle-flux vector, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_{0,a}$ is the velocity distribution for the selected neutral species and internal state. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, $a$ labels the internal quantum state, and $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal component. The integral covers all velocities. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ specifies the positive local poloidal direction in a constant-toroidal-angle plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Its poloidal orientation must be specified.

The quantity includes thermal and nonthermal particles in the selected state, without summing over species or internal states. It is local, not surface-integrated or surface-averaged. Summing over an exhaustive, nonoverlapping set of internal states gives the [poloidal neutral particle flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux) of the same species.

It specializes [neutral internal-state particle flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) to a surface whose normal is the local poloidal direction. This geometric projection is distinct from the [parallel neutral internal-state particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux), whose direction follows the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral particles in the selected internal state have net number transport along $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

items.name: total_absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to all plasma particle populations and integrated over all spatial locations.
items.documentation:
Total absorbed wave power is the total rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to all plasma particle populations, with contributions integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the combined energy of all included plasma particle populations, $t$ is time, and the subscript “waves” restricts the derivative to direct energy transfer from the coherent electromagnetic-wave field.

This quantity is globally aggregated: it is summed over all species, charge states, populations, and spatial locations. It includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes electromagnetic power that remains in the wave field and energy subsequently redistributed between particle populations by collisions.

It is the species-summed specialization of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), unlike [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power), which is restricted to electron populations. It is also the global counterpart of [total absorbed wave power at the inside flux surface](name:total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface), which retains only the power enclosed within a selected flux surface; Fourier-resolved contributions are represented by [per-toroidal-mode total absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: diamagnetic_energy
items.description: Diamagnetic energy measures plasma stored energy as three-halves of the volume-integrated pressure perpendicular to the magnetic field, including thermal and fast-particle contributions.
items.documentation:
Diamagnetic energy is the global plasma stored-energy measure associated with total pressure perpendicular to the local magnetic field. It includes both thermal and fast-particle pressure contributions.

The diamagnetic energy $W_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is defined by:

$$
W_{\mathrm{dia}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_V p_\perp\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a physical volume element, and $p_\perp$ is the total perpendicular pressure, summed over all contributing plasma species, charge states, and thermal and fast-particle populations. The integral covers the full plasma volume rather than a selected species or local region.

For isotropic total pressure, this definition gives the corresponding isotropic MHD stored energy. In the isotropic, purely thermal limit, it equals the [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy). It is not restricted to thermal energy and, when the pressure is anisotropic, is not generally equal to the total particle kinetic energy.

The [time derivative of diamagnetic energy](name:time_derivative_of_diamagnetic_energy) is the rate of change of this global energy content.

items.name: thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description: Volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer vector delivered to the electron population by Coulomb collisions with other plasma species.
items.documentation:
Electron collisional torque is the volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer to an electron population caused by Coulomb collisions with other plasma species. It represents collisional momentum exchange rather than a local torque density.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the total collisional torque, $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is displacement from the torque origin, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density acting on electrons. The quantity excludes torque from external sources and noncollisional interactions. Its components include the [toroidal thermal-electron torque](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions), while toroidal fast-electron torque resolves the corresponding exchange for a nonthermal population; the family is represented by [electron torque due to collisions](name:electron_torque_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when a component points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

items.name: vertical_outline_of_vacuum_vessel
items.description: Signed vertical position of a point on a vacuum-vessel element outline, measured along the vertical axis of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the vertical coordinate of a specified point on the geometric outline of a vacuum-vessel element. It identifies the point's height relative to the cylindrical coordinate origin, rather than an element center, thickness, or surface-normal displacement.

The coordinate is defined by projection of the point position onto the vertical basis vector:

$$
Z_{\rm point}=\mathbf{r}_{\rm point}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_{\rm point}$ is the position vector of the outline point, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector, and $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed cylindrical frame with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical coordinate.

Sign convention: Positive when the outline point lies in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping
items.description: Global rate of particle-number removal from the plasma by pumping through the wall, aggregated over carrier species and charge states rather than resolved as an areal flux.
items.documentation:
The particle pumping rate is the global throughput of particles removed from the plasma at the wall by pumping. It represents particle number, not energy or momentum, and is not an areal flux density.

The rate is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{p,pump}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{p,removed}}}{dt}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{p,pump}}$ is the particle-number removal rate due to pumping, $N_{\mathrm{p,removed}}$ is the cumulative number of particles removed through the wall by pumping, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies globally over the wall and aggregates the removed particle population without selecting a species or charge state. It is not resolved by wall area or position and does not represent a neutral-only rate or an electron-equivalent rate.

The explicit particle channel identifies the removed particle-number throughput within the broader pumping-rate family. It has the same global wall and pumping scope as [rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping](name:rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping), while distinguishing particle-number removal from any other transport channel.

items.name: cumulative_inside_flux_surface_electron_particle_source_rate
items.description: Cumulative electron particle source rate is the net production or removal of free electrons integrated over the plasma volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Cumulative electron particle source rate is the net rate at which source and sink processes add or remove free electrons within the plasma volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface. It supplies the source contribution to the enclosed electron-number balance.

The enclosed rate is defined by

$$
S_{e,\mathrm{inside}}(\psi)=\int_{V(\psi)} S_{e,\mathrm{vol}}\,dV
$$

where $S_{e,\mathrm{inside}}$ is the cumulative electron particle source rate, $\psi$ labels the enclosing magnetic flux surface, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed plasma region, $S_{e,\mathrm{vol}}$ is the local net [electron volumetric source rate](name:electron_volumetric_source_rate), and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

The integral retains the electron source contribution under consideration and imposes no thermal-population or orbit-class restriction. It accumulates the source over space, not time, and is neither a flux-surface average nor a volume-normalized rate. Transport through the enclosing surface contributes separately to electron-number balance, so this source rate is not generally the time derivative of the enclosed electron inventory.

The [cumulative ion charge-state source rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate) uses the same enclosed-volume integration but counts ions in a specified charge state rather than free electrons.

Sign convention: Positive when the enclosed source contribution produces a net gain of free electrons; negative values indicate net loss.

items.name: neutral_energy_flux
items.description: Neutral energy flux is the signed component of energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules normal to an oriented surface, summed over neutral species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral energy flux is the signed surface-normal component of energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules. It describes local energy transport across an oriented surface, rather than the magnitude of the full energy-flux vector, and is the neutral-population specialization of [energy flux].

For an oriented surface, the scalar flux is the projection of the total neutral energy-flux-density vector onto its unit normal:

$$
\Gamma_{0,W} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,W} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}
$$

Here, $\Gamma_{0,W}$ is the signed neutral energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,W}$ is the total neutral energy-flux-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface unit normal. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population, and $W$ denotes the energy channel.

At a given location, contributions are summed over all neutral species and internal states, not averaged. The [neutral species energy flux](name:neutral_species_energy_flux) resolves the species contributions, while [neutral internal-state energy flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) restricts the energy transport to a specified internal state. Energy carried by charged particles or radiation is excluded. Unlike [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux), this quantity describes energy transport rather than particle-number transport; it is a local flux density, not surface-integrated power.

The [radial neutral energy flux](name:radial_neutral_energy_flux) selects the projection along $\hat R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat R, \hat\phi, \hat Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The [parallel neutral energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux) selects the projection along the local magnetic-field direction. These are direction-specific forms of the same neutral energy transport, not components to sum to obtain the parent quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral energy transport is directed along the chosen surface normal.

items.name: runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer
items.description: Runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation is the volumetric rate at which parallel electric acceleration drives electrons from the thermal distribution's suprathermal tail into runaway motion.
items.documentation:
Runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation is the volumetric production rate of electrons entering the runaway population through primary electric-field acceleration from the thermal distribution's suprathermal tail. Acceleration by the electric-field component parallel to the magnetic field carries these electrons across the critical boundary beyond which electric acceleration overcomes collisional friction.

The local kinetic definition is the velocity-space particle flux across that boundary into the runaway population:

$$
S_{\mathrm{D}} = \int_{\Sigma_c} \boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{D}}_v \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_v \, dA_v
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation, $\Sigma_c$ is the critical boundary in electron velocity space, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{D}}_v$ is the Dreicer velocity-space particle flux associated with parallel electric acceleration and Coulomb collisions, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_v$ is the unit normal directed into the runaway region, and $dA_v$ is an area element of that boundary.

This quantity counts transfer into the runaway population, not creation of additional electrons or the net time derivative of runaway-electron density. It excludes avalanche multiplication, [hot-tail production](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), and other non-Dreicer sources. It is distinct from the [fast-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation] unless the fast-electron population is defined to coincide with the runaway population.

No spatial averaging is implied by the unqualified quantity. The [volume-averaged runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer) is its integral over the plasma volume divided by that volume; it retains the same mechanism and population scope.

items.name: diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description: Electric-current contribution along the local diamagnetic direction, driven by heat-viscosity stresses in a collisional magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
The diamagnetic heat-viscosity current density is the local diamagnetic-direction contribution to electric current generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure. The diamagnetic label selects the direction, while heat viscosity identifies the driving mechanism.

Its defining directional decomposition is

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}, \qquad
\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv,dia}} = j_{\mathrm{dia}}\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the signed diamagnetic component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the local diamagnetic unit vector, and $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv,dia}}$ is the corresponding vector contribution. The diamagnetic direction is perpendicular to the local magnetic field. Its orientation requires a reference gradient or surface normal; the magnetic-field direction alone does not determine it, and the supplied definition does not specify that reference.

This is a local, mechanism-resolved contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not a spatial average or an integrated current. It is neither the entire perpendicular current nor the full pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current. The [parallel heat-viscosity current density](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) is the magnetic-field-aligned projection of the same parent vector rather than its diamagnetic projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the heat-viscosity conventional-current contribution projects along the chosen positive local diamagnetic unit vector.

items.name: parallel_electron_energy_flux
items.description: Parallel electron energy flux is the signed rate of electron kinetic-energy transport per unit area through a surface perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Parallel electron energy flux represents net kinetic-energy transport by electrons along the local magnetic field. It is the field-aligned component of [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux).

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{e,W,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,W,\parallel}$ is the signed parallel electron energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}$ is the electron kinetic-energy flux vector, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The subscripts $e$ and $W$ identify the electron population and energy transport channel, respectively.

This quantity includes the total electron energy-transport contribution along the field rather than only its diffusive or convective part. It excludes perpendicular electron energy transport and energy carried by other species; no spatial integration or averaging is implied. The [parallel electron energy diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity) characterizes the gradient-driven diffusive contribution, not the total flux defined here.

Sign convention: Positive when net electron kinetic-energy transport is in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: neutral_power_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description: Power deposited on plasma-facing wall surfaces when incident neutral hydrogen-isotope particles recombine at the material surface, primarily through molecular formation and release of binding energy.
items.documentation:
Neutral surface-recombination power at the wall is the rate at which recombination energy from incident neutral particles is deposited in plasma-facing wall material. It represents the neutral-channel contribution to the wall heat load from recombination.

The deposited power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{rec,wall}}^{\mathrm{neutral}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} \sum_r \Gamma_r Q_r \, \mathrm{d}A
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the set of plasma-facing wall surfaces, $r$ indexes neutral surface-recombination channels, $\Gamma_r$ is the corresponding recombination-event rate per unit area, and $Q_r$ is the energy deposited per event. The quantity is the neutral component of [power at wall due to recombination](name:power_at_wall_due_to_recombination), complementary to [plasma power at wall due to recombination](name:plasma_power_at_wall_due_to_recombination); plasma-ion electron-capture recombination is excluded.

items.name: effective_neutral_diffusivity
items.description: Direction-resolved effective Fickian diffusivity relating neutral-particle diffusive flux to the corresponding neutral-density gradient.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the direction-resolved effective Fickian diffusivity for neutral-particle transport. It retains directional components that are not represented by the scalar neutral diffusivity.

For each resolved direction $k$, the diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,k}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{n,k}^{\mathrm{eff}}\,\partial_k n_n
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,k}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the neutral-particle diffusive flux component, $D_{n,k}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the corresponding effective diffusivity component, $\partial_k$ is the spatial derivative in direction $k$, and $n_n$ is the neutral-particle number density.

The quantity excludes convective transport and particle sources or sinks. Its radial component is represented by [radial effective neutral diffusivity](name:radial_effective_neutral_diffusivity); passive down-gradient diffusion has nonnegative effective coefficients.

items.name: ion_charge_state_power_density
items.description: Net volumetric rate of energy transfer to or from ions of a specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle, summed over the included energy-source and loss processes.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from ions of a specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle per unit physical volume. It is the source or sink term for that recipient population in its energy transport equation.

The volumetric source is defined by

$$
p_{s,\mathcal B} = \frac{dP_{s,\mathcal B}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{s,\mathcal B}$ is the ion charge-state power density, $P_{s,\mathcal B}$ is the signed net power transferred to the selected ions, $V$ is physical volume, $s$ identifies the ion species, and $\mathcal B$ denotes the selected charge state or set of charge states forming a bundle.

Contributions are summed over the charge states within the bundle and over the included energy-transfer processes, not averaged over charge states. Other species and charge states outside the bundle are excluded. The definition applies locally; a flux-surface-averaged form averages this same volumetric source over the specified magnetic flux surface. Neither form is stored energy or volume-integrated power.

The quantity is not restricted to wave absorption or to thermal or fast ions. The [fast-ion charge-state power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) and [thermal-ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) specialize it to wave energy deposition into their respective recipient populations. Summing over a complete, nonoverlapping partition of a species' ionic charge states gives its [ion power density](name:ion_power_density), provided the recipient populations, included processes, and spatial averaging are the same.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred to the selected ion charge state or charge-state bundle.

items.name: parallel_ion_velocity
items.description: Charge-state-averaged ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the local magnetic-field direction, using the density-weighted first velocity moment of all included ionization charge states.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion velocity represents the local magnetic-field-aligned component of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk flow. It is the field-aligned resolution of [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity), rather than the velocity of a single ionization charge state.

$$
V_{i,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf V_i=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\frac{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}\mathbf V_{i,Z}}{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}}
$$

Here $V_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion velocity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf V_i$ is the charge-state-averaged ion velocity, $n_{i,Z}$ is the number density of ion charge state $Z$, and $\mathbf V_{i,Z}$ is that charge state's bulk velocity. The sum includes all included ionization charge states. Unlike [parallel ion charge-state velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity), this quantity is not resolved to one selected charge state; it complements geometric components such as [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when the ion flow points along the local magnetic-field direction.

items.name: toroidal_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Toroidal flux limiter coefficient is the dimensionless factor that caps neutral-particle-state momentum flux at its collisionless free-streaming bound while preserving the toroidal flux sign.
items.documentation:
Toroidal flux limiter coefficient is the dimensionless factor that scales the collisionless free-streaming bound on the toroidal component of neutral-particle-state momentum flux in a multi-fluid transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the sign assigned to that toroidal flux component.

For the toroidal component, the direction-preserving limited flux is defined by

$$
F_\phi = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_\phi^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_\phi^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_\phi F_\phi^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_\phi$ is the limited toroidal momentum-flux density, $F_\phi^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure flux, $F_\phi^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming bound, and $L_\phi$ is this toroidal flux limiter coefficient.

This quantity is the toroidal component of the generic [flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient) and is distinct from the poloidal component represented by [poloidal flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient). It limits momentum flux rather than defining the flux itself.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated toroidal momentum flux points along $+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: torque_density_due_to_thermalization
items.description: Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume caused by particle thermalization into the thermal plasma, with sign set by the transfer direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local source or sink of angular momentum transferred to the thermal plasma when non-thermal particles thermalize. It represents the rate at which thermalization changes the angular-momentum density of the receiving population.

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{th}} = \left(\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the torque density due to thermalization, $\ell$ is the represented component of angular-momentum density, and $t$ is time. The quantity includes only transfer attributable to thermalization, excluding independently attributed collisional, electromagnetic, or external-source contributions. The ion-specific instance is [ion torque density due to thermalization](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization). It may be negative when thermalization removes angular momentum from the receiving thermal population, including when thermal particles are accelerated into a distinct non-thermal population.

Sign convention: Positive when thermalization increases the represented angular-momentum component in its positive physical orientation.

items.name: perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Local mean of the two kinetic stresses perpendicular to the magnetic field, carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits.
items.documentation:
Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the local gyrotropic kinetic-pressure component perpendicular to the magnetic field, carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is distinct from the scalar trace pressure of that population.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, its kinetic moment is:

$$
p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} \frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\,f_{s,c,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

Here, $p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,fast}}$ is the perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure; $s$ labels particle species; $c$ labels charge state; $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; $f_{s,c,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution for species $s$ and charge state $c$; and $\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the set of velocities at $\mathbf{x}$ corresponding to trapped orbits. The element $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The perpendicular speed is $v_\perp=|\mathbf{v}-(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|$, where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector. The factor of one half gives the mean over the two perpendicular velocity directions.

The local quantity applies at points in the poloidal plane and may vary along a magnetic flux surface; a flux-surface average is an average of these local values. Contributions are summed over all suprathermal particle species and over all charge states of each species. Trapped particles reverse their field-parallel motion at magnetic mirror points. Thermal particles and passing particles, including co-passing and counter-passing populations, are excluded. Perpendicular is relative to the magnetic-field direction, not the normal to a flux surface.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), distinct from the [perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure). For the same trapped population at the same location, [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) is the scalar trace pressure: one third of the sum of the [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure) and twice this perpendicular component.

items.name: x_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera
items.description: X-axis component of a camera’s image-up orientation unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The camera image-up orientation is represented by a unit vector that defines the upward direction of the camera image in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame. This orientation is distinct from the [camera line-of-sight direction](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).

The quantity is the projection of the image-up unit vector onto the Cartesian x-axis:

$$
u_x = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{up}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{x}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{up}}$ is the camera image-up orientation unit vector and $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $x$. Together with the [y image-up component](name:y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera) and z image-up component, it specifies the image-up orientation.

items.name: ion_heating_power
items.description: Net rate of energy deposition into the ion population from all heating sources and mechanisms, aggregated over all ion species.
items.documentation:
Ion heating power quantifies the total power flowing into the collective ion population from all external and internal sources, including neutral beam thermalization, radiofrequency absorption at ion cyclotron resonances, and collisional energy transfer from suprathermal particles and electrons. It represents the ion-population component of the total heating_power, partitioned from the electron heating channel by the coupled energy-balance equations.

The quantity is the volume integral of the local ion heating power density $S_i$ summed over all ion species and all active heating mechanisms:

$$
P_{\rm ion} = \int_V S_i \, dV
$$

where $S_i$ (in W m$^{-3}$) encompasses every ion heating process and $V$ is the plasma volume over which the integration is performed.

In power-balance analysis, $P_{\rm ion}$ is inferred by combining ion temperature profile measurements with transport modeling to close the ion energy equation. When a flux-surface-resolved cumulative form is required, total_ion_heating_power_at_inside_flux_surface provides the profile integrated inside each enclosed flux surface, and [total_ion_heating_power](name:total_ion_heating_power) gives the full-volume aggregate. For contributions attributed to a specific mechanism, [total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating) isolates the ion cyclotron resonance channel. The thermalized ion subpopulation contribution resolved against flux-surface volume is tracked by [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fickian diffusion coefficient for radial transport of thermal energy by the aggregated neutral particle population in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral energy diffusion coefficient characterizes the proportionality between the radial diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux and the major-radius gradient of neutral thermal-energy density in an edge plasma. Neutral transport is not constrained to magnetic-field lines, and this coefficient is the radial component of the directionally resolved neutral transport.

The Fickian closure is

$$
q_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{n,R}^{E}\frac{\partial}{\partial R}\left(\frac{3}{2}n_n T_n\right)
$$

where $q_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux, $D_{n,R}^{E}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $n_n$ is neutral number density, and $T_n$ is neutral temperature.

This coefficient is the radial component of the parent [neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and applies to the aggregated neutral population. Directional comparison is provided by the [poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), while state-resolved transport is represented by [radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: parallel_ion_current_density
items.description: Parallel ion current density is the signed conventional charge flux carried by ions along the local magnetic field at a plasma-facing surface.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion current density at a plasma-facing surface is the signed projection of the [ion current density](name:ion_current_density) onto the local magnetic-field direction. It is the ion-carried, field-aligned contribution to [current density](name:current_density).

The projection and its charge-weighted particle-flux representation are:

$$
j_{i,\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_i = \sum_{s,z} q_{s,z}\,\Gamma_{s,z,\parallel}
$$

where $j_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion current density, $\mathbf{j}_i$ is the ion current-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$, whose magnitude is $|\mathbf{B}|$. The indices $s$ and $z$ identify ion species and ionic charge states, $q_{s,z}$ is the electric charge of each ion in that population, and $\Gamma_{s,z,\parallel}$ is its [parallel ion charge-state particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux).

The quantity applies locally at the plasma-facing surface and sums the charge-weighted contributions of all included ion species and charge states. Electron current is excluded, distinguishing it from species-unrestricted [parallel current density]. It is neither a flux-surface average nor a surface-integrated current. The parallel direction follows the magnetic field, not the material-surface normal; these projections coincide only when the field and surface-normal directions coincide.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional electric current carried by ions flows along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description: Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the signed charge flux along the local magnetic field generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a collisional magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the local magnetic-field-aligned component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_{\parallel} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_{\parallel}$ is this signed parallel current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. Specifically, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its nonzero magnitude.

This quantity is the net conventional charge flux attributed to heat viscosity in the edge plasma, combining the charged-species contributions rather than selecting one species. It is a local signed component, not a current magnitude, a flux-surface average, or the total current density from all mechanisms.

The [vertical heat-viscosity current density](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) is a different projection of the same parent vector. By contrast, [parallel current density due to parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) has the same projection direction but represents a distinct viscous-stress contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the heat-viscosity contribution to conventional electric current flows along the local magnetic field.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from fast or non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state, including all donor orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from a fast or non-Maxwellian particle population to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state. It is an energy-exchange source or sink for the receiving thermal population, not its stored kinetic-energy density.

The receiving population's kinetic-energy moment defines this contribution:

$$
P_{i,z,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{D}} \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iz,a}\bigl(f_{iz}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a\bigr)(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i,z,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $i$ identifies the receiving ion species, $z$ is its charge number, and $m_i$ is its particle mass. The vector $\mathbf{v}$ is the receiving ion velocity, $v$ is its magnitude, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration element. The distribution $f_{iz}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes the receiving thermal ions, $f_a$ describes donor species $a$, and $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of species in the designated fast or non-Maxwellian donor population. The operator $C_{iz,a}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the receiving distribution caused by Coulomb interactions with that donor species.

The donor contribution includes co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit classes. There is no sum over receiving ion charge states and no orbit-class restriction on the thermal recipients. The local definition imposes no flux-surface averaging. Energy transferred to fast ions or electrons is excluded.

This is the thermal-recipient component of [ion charge-state collisional power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), rather than the combined thermal- and fast-ion contribution. The donor orbit-class contributions sum to this quantity locally. Flux-surface averaging those contributions gives the corresponding orbit-resolved averages, including [co-passing thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic-energy density of the specified thermal-ion charge-state population.

items.name: co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Local rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer from co-passing fast particles to a specified fast-ion species, summed over all of that species’ ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Co-passing fast-ion collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from co-passing fast particles to a specified fast-ion species. The co-passing restriction identifies the donor particles’ passing orbit class; it does not restrict the receiving fast ions to that class.

For receiving ion species $i$, the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator defines the quantity:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{q\in Q_i} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{1}{2}m_{iq}|\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{fast}},f_{f,\mathrm{co}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this power density; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $i$ identifies the receiving fast-ion species; $Q_i$ is the set of its ionic charge states; $q$ identifies one such charge state; $m_{iq}$ is the mass of ions in that state; $\mathbf{v}$ is receiving-ion velocity; $|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed; $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the receiving fast-ion distribution; and $f_{f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the distribution of donor fast particles in the co-passing orbit class. The operator $C_{iq\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}$ gives the collisional rate of change of the receiving distribution due to Coulomb collisions with those donors, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral spans the full receiving-ion velocity space.

The quantity is summed over all charge states of the specified receiving ion species, not averaged over charge states or summed over different receiving species. Co-passing restricts the donor fast particles; counter-passing and trapped donors are excluded. This is a local energy-transfer rate per volume, not stored kinetic-energy density or volume-integrated power, and it excludes energy transfer to the bulk thermal-ion population. The [charge-state-resolved counterpart](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) specifies one receiving ionic charge state rather than summing over charge states.

This is the co-passing donor-orbit contribution to [fast-ion collisional power density](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). Together with the [counter-passing contribution](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and the [trapped contribution](name:trapped_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), it forms the orbit-class sum for fast-ion collisional power density.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the co-passing fast-particle population to the receiving fast-ion population.

items.name: implicit_ion_energy_source_rate
items.description: Implicit ion energy source rate is the coefficient multiplying ion temperature in the stiff, proportional contribution to an ion energy source or sink.
items.documentation:
Implicit ion energy source rate is the proportional coefficient in the stiff part of a decomposed ion energy source or sink. It multiplies the temperature of the ion population whose energy balance is being described.

In the temperature form of that energy balance, the defining decomposition is:

$$
\mathcal{S}_{i,W} = \mathcal{S}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{exp}} + S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{imp}} T_i
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_{i,W}$ is the complete source contribution to the ion-temperature evolution, $\mathcal{S}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is its explicitly treated remainder, $S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit coefficient defined here, and $T_i$ is the ion temperature. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion population, and $W$ identifies the energy channel. The decomposition is a linearized representation of the source, not a separation into distinct physical mechanisms.

The coefficient applies to the specified ion population and source contribution; an all-species total is not implied. The [total implicit ion energy source rate](name:total_implicit_ion_energy_source_rate) specializes this quantity to the aggregate ion energy balance, whereas the [implicit ion-state energy source rate](name:implicit_ion_state_energy_source_rate) resolves an individual ion charge state. An aggregate coefficient belongs to the aggregate balance and is not generally an unweighted sum of species coefficients.

This coefficient is not a heating power or power density. Its product with ion temperature gives only the proportional contribution; the explicit remainder must also be included to obtain the complete source or sink.

Sign convention: Positive when the proportional contribution adds energy to the specified ion population, and negative when it removes energy.

items.name: neutral_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient relating neutral-particle transport to neutral number-density gradients, with components resolved along the relevant transport directions.
items.documentation:
Neutral particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by a neutral number-density gradient. It is the neutral-population specialization of [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), without selecting a transport direction.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive neutral-particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_i\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n}}}{\partial s_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive neutral-particle flux component, $D_i$ is the corresponding component of neutral particle diffusivity, $n_{\mathrm{n}}$ is neutral particle number density, and $s_i$ is physical arclength along the resolved direction. The minus sign specifies transport down the number-density gradient.

This parent covers directional components such as [parallel neutral particle diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity) and [poloidal neutral particle diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity). It does not select a particular neutral chemical species or internal state; those population refinements are represented by [neutral species particle diffusivity](name:neutral_species_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed equilibrium flux through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle at that location.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle at that location. It is the magnetic-axis value of the equilibrium [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, its defining relation is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a} = \Phi_{\mathrm{p}}(R_a,Z_a) = 2\pi \int_0^{R_a} B_Z(R',Z_a)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a}$ is the magnetic-axis poloidal flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function, $R_a$ and $Z_a$ are the magnetic-axis coordinates, $R'$ is the major-radius integration variable, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component.

This value includes both externally generated and plasma-current-generated flux; it is not an external-source-only contribution. It is an unnormalized flux value and need not vanish at the magnetic axis.

Together with the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), denoted by $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}$, it defines the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},N} = (\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a})/(\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a})$. This coordinate is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the plasma boundary, provided the two reference flux values differ. These physical reference endpoints apply even when the flux-coordinate interval under consideration does not extend to the axis or boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic field threading the integration disk is directed toward increasing $Z$.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: neutral_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Effective convection velocity assigned to the diamagnetic contribution to neutral-species momentum transport, retaining the direction of transport.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective convection-velocity vector assigned to the diamagnetic contribution to momentum transport of a selected neutral species. It is a transport coefficient, not an intrinsic magnetic drift of electrically neutral particles.

Its role in a convective momentum closure is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{P_0,*}=P_0\mathbf{v}_{0,*}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{0,*}$ is the effective diamagnetic convection velocity, $P_0$ is the transported component of neutral-species momentum density, and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{P_0,*}$ is the corresponding diamagnetic contribution to its convective momentum flux. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population, and the asterisk labels the diamagnetic contribution. The transported momentum component and the direction of its transport are distinct.

The coefficient applies to one neutral species without resolving its internal states, unlike the [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It is not a sum over different neutral species and excludes ionic charge states.

The parent [velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:perpendicular_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) establishes the pressure-gradient-associated attribution. For neutrals, that attribution denotes an effective transport contribution; the charged-particle diamagnetic drift formula does not apply because the particle charge is zero. This coefficient is distinct from the total neutral bulk-flow velocity.

The [neutral velocity magnitude due to diamagnetic drift] is the Euclidean norm of this vector and therefore omits its transport direction.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of the effective convection velocity points along its specified positive transport direction.

items.name: parallel_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Field-aligned projection of the effective diamagnetic pressure-gradient velocity contribution assigned to one internal state of a neutral species in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the field-aligned projection of an effective pressure-gradient transport contribution assigned to one neutral atomic or molecular internal quantum state in the edge plasma. It represents an effective fluid contribution, not a direct magnetic drift of individual neutral particles.

For the selected neutral state, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s}^{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $s$ labels the selected internal state of the specified neutral species, $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\parallel}$ is its parallel velocity contribution, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is its effective diamagnetic pressure-gradient velocity contribution, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

The quantity is state resolved, with no sum or average over internal states or neutral species. It excludes independent parallel-flow contributions and is not the total [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). Because neutral particles carry no charge, the charged-particle diamagnetic-drift formula does not directly define this effective neutral contribution.

This quantity is the field-parallel specialization of [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), whereas [perpendicular neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:perpendicular_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) selects a direction perpendicular to the magnetic field. If the assigned effective contribution is purely perpendicular, its parallel projection is zero.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective neutral-state velocity contribution has a component along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Signed toroidal component of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma onto the toroidal direction. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For ion charge state $\alpha$ with scalar partial pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\phi} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\phi}$ is the toroidal diamagnetic velocity component, $p_\alpha$ is the partial pressure of that charge state, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $q_\alpha$ is its particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is its number density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The unit vector $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the distance from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is local and charge-state resolved, with no sum or average over charge states. It excludes electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent parallel flow; it is not the total ion velocity or an angular rotation rate. Its toroidal projection can be nonzero even though the diamagnetic drift is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

Unlike the [binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which projects the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states onto the local binormal direction, this quantity selects one charge state and the geometric toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid velocity has a component toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: ion_state_mean_ionisation_potential
items.description: Concentration-weighted mean cumulative ionization energy required to reach the charge states represented in a charge-state bundle of one ion species from the neutral ground state.
items.documentation:
Ion-state mean ionization potential is the concentration-weighted mean cumulative ionization energy of an ion charge-state bundle. For each represented charge state, the cumulative energy is the sum of successive ionization energies needed to reach it from the neutral ground state of the same species.

The mean cumulative ionization energy is defined by:

$$
\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{B}_s} x_z \left(\sum_{k=0}^{z-1} I_k\right)
$$

where $\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}$ is the mean for bundle $s$, $\mathcal{B}_s$ is the set of charge numbers represented in that bundle, $z$ is a represented ionic charge number, and $x_z$ is the relative number concentration of charge state $z$ within the bundle. The fractions satisfy $x_z\geq 0$ and $\sum_{z\in\mathcal{B}_s}x_z=1$. The index $k$ labels an intermediate charge number, and $I_k$ is the ground-state ionization energy required to remove an electron from charge state $k$ and produce charge state $k+1$; the cumulative sum for the neutral state is zero.

The quantity is a density-weighted mean over the charge states represented in the bundle of one ion species, not necessarily over every charge state of that species. It is a mean per particle, not an energy summed over the bundle population; for a bundle containing one charge state, it equals that state's cumulative ionization energy, not the threshold for its next ionization step. It excludes thermal internal energy, excitation energy, radiation losses, and kinetic energy exchanged during ionization or recombination. The [maximum ion charge number](name:ion_state_maximum_charge_number) identifies the highest charge state included in the bundle.

The [change in ion-state mean ionization potential] is the value of this bundle mean after a specified state change minus its value before the change.

items.name: electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the diffusive thermal energy flux of the electron population to the local electron temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
items.documentation:
The electron energy diffusion coefficient $D_{e,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the electron population, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the diffusive electron heat flux and the local electron temperature gradient. It is the electron-species-resolved instance of the parent [energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective or $E \times B$ drift contributions to the total electron heat flux.

The defining relation for the diffusive electron heat flux $\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{diff}}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,E} \, \nabla T_e
$$

where $D_{e,E}$ is the electron energy diffusion coefficient and $T_e$ is the local electron temperature. In a magnetized plasma $D_{e,E}$ is strongly anisotropic; cross-field radial values govern electron energy confinement while values along field lines are many orders of magnitude larger.

Directional projections of this coefficient include [radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient), which governs cross-field energy confinement, and poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient, which captures transport along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The analogous coefficient for the ion population is given by [ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: requested_voltage_of_neutron_detector
items.description: Voltage of a neutron detector specified as a power-supply setpoint: the target bias voltage for a high-voltage supply or the target electronics-operating voltage for a low-voltage supply, distinct from the measured supply output.
items.documentation:
Voltage of neutron detector

The requested voltage $U$ is the difference between the target potential at the supply output and the potential at its reference terminal:

$$
U = \Phi_{\mathrm{set}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $U$ is the commanded supply-voltage setpoint, $\Phi_{\mathrm{set}}$ is the target electric potential of the supply output terminal, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the electric potential of the supply reference terminal; both potentials use the same potential origin.

For a neutron detector, this is the high-voltage supply setpoint for target detector bias or the low-voltage supply setpoint for detector electronics operation. It is specific to one supply, not a sum or average of the high- and low-voltage settings or a value aggregated across detectors. It denotes the commanded target, not the measured supply output or the detector signal represented by [voltage of a neutron detector].

Its commanded-setpoint role is analogous to the [requested voltage of a spectrometer channel](name:requested_voltage_of_spectrometer_channel), with the distinction that this quantity applies to a neutron detector. It is distinct from the applied detector-bias voltage represented by [voltage of a mass spectrometer](name:voltage_of_mass_spectrometer).

Sign convention: Positive when the target potential at the supply output terminal exceeds the potential at the supply reference terminal.

items.name: tritium_tritium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion
items.description: Total neutron production rate from the thermonuclear tritium-tritium reaction branch among Maxwellian bulk tritons, excluding beam-target and beam-beam fast-ion contributions.
items.documentation:
The total neutron source rate due to thermal fusion is the number of neutrons produced per unit time by the thermal tritium-tritium reaction branch between bulk tritons with locally Maxwellian velocity distributions. It is the tritium-tritium channel member of [neutron source rate due to thermal fusion](name:neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion) and contributes to the channel-summed [total neutron source rate due to thermal fusion](name:total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

The tritium-tritium thermal neutron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,TT}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_V 2\,\frac{n_T^2}{2}\,\langle\sigma v\rangle_{TT}(T_T)\,dV
$$

where $S_{n,TT}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the source rate, $V$ is the emitting plasma volume, $n_T$ is the local bulk triton number density, $\langle\sigma v\rangle_{TT}$ is the Maxwellian-averaged tritium-tritium fusion reactivity, $T_T$ is the local triton temperature, and $dV$ is a volume element. The factor of two is the neutron multiplicity of the tritium-tritium branch, while the denominator prevents double counting identical triton pairs.

Only reactions between locally Maxwellian bulk tritons are included; beam-target, beam-beam, fusion-product, and other nonthermal fast-ion contributions are excluded. The deuterium-deuterium channel, including its neutron-producing branch, is a separate contribution described by [deuterium-deuterium neutron source rate due to thermal fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

items.name: parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective velocity coefficient relating neutral energy density to its directed convective flux along the local magnetic field in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral-energy convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the energy-density-proportional advective flux carried by neutral particles along the local magnetic field. It describes directed energy transport after gradient-driven transport has been separated.

The parallel convective neutral-energy flux is defined by

$$
Q_{n,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = U_n v_{n,\parallel}^{E}
$$

where $Q_{n,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-parallel convective neutral-energy flux, $U_n$ is the energy density of the neutral population represented in the energy balance, and $v_{n,\parallel}^{E}$ is this effective convection velocity.

The parallel projection is $v_{n,\parallel}^{E}=\mathbf v_n^{E}\cdot\mathbf b$, where $\mathbf v_n^{E}$ is the effective neutral-energy convection velocity vector and $\mathbf b=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The quantity applies to the specified neutral population in the edge plasma; it is an energy-channel coefficient, not a sum of particle or momentum transport coefficients.

The quantity excludes conductive and diffusive energy transport and need not equal the bulk neutral flow velocity. It describes field-parallel transport, rather than the transport across magnetic flux surfaces represented by [neutral energy convection velocity](name:neutral_energy_convection_velocity). It is also distinct from [ion heat convection velocity](name:ion_heat_convection_velocity), which acts on ion thermal energy rather than neutral energy.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral-energy convection velocity points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_constraint_position
items.description: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the constraint position labels its magnetic surface by the square root of the axis-to-boundary toroidal-flux fraction.
items.documentation:
Normalized toroidal flux coordinate

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}/\rho_{\mathrm{tor,b}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the constraint position, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate of the magnetic surface containing that position, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,b}}$ is the [toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary).

Within the nested closed-flux-surface region, the label ranges from zero at the magnetic axis to one at the equilibrium boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It is evaluated at one specified constraint position, not averaged over constraint positions. It is neither a geometric distance nor the value of the constrained physical quantity.

This quantity is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). When the equilibrium boundary is a separatrix, its boundary value equals the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the separatrix](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_separatrix).

items.name: trapped_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume from trapped nonthermal particles to thermal ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed rate of kinetic-energy transfer per unit volume from trapped fast or non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions of a specified species, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Trapped particles undergo magnetic reflection rather than continuous passing motion; the orbit restriction applies to the donating distribution, not to the recipient thermal ions.

The power transferred to the thermal ion species is defined by

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_z \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iz,a}[f_{iz}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}]\,d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the trapped-source thermal-ion collisional power density, $i$ identifies the recipient ion species, $z$ labels its ionic charge states, and $a$ labels the donating nonthermal species. The mass $m_i$ is the recipient ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient velocity, and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed; the integral covers all recipient velocities. The distributions $f_{iz}^{\mathrm{th}}$ and $f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}$ describe the thermal recipient charge state and the trapped donating population, respectively. The Coulomb collision operator $C_{iz,a}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the recipient distribution due to that donor. Angle brackets denote a flux-surface average, defined as the limiting volume average over an infinitesimally thin shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The charge-state sum includes all ionic charge states of the specified species and excludes neutrals; it is a sum of power contributions, not a density-weighted mean. The [trapped thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding single-charge-state contribution. This quantity excludes energy transferred to fast ions or electrons and is neither stored kinetic-energy density nor volume-integrated power.

This is the trapped-source contribution to [thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). With the same flux-surface averaging, adding the co-passing and counter-passing source contributions recovers the orbit-unrestricted thermal-ion collisional power density.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic energy from the trapped nonthermal distribution to the thermal ion population; negative when the net transfer is reversed.

items.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective convection coefficient relating the flux of vertical momentum across an oriented surface to its density for one neutral species in one resolved internal state.
items.documentation:
The vertical neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity is the effective coefficient governing non-diffusive transport of vertical [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one neutral species in one specified internal state. Vertical denotes the momentum component parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The transport direction is normal to the oriented transport surface and need not be vertical.

The density-proportional convective contribution is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}\,g_{0a,Z}
$$

where $\Pi_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the signed flux of vertical momentum through the oriented surface, $V_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection coefficient, and $g_{0a,Z}$ is the vertical momentum density. The subscript $0$ denotes the selected neutral population, $a$ labels its internal state, and the superscript $\mathrm{conv}$ identifies the convective contribution.

This coefficient resolves the vertical-momentum channel of the [effective neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection). It applies to one species and one internal state, without summing or averaging over either. It is a transport-closure coefficient, not necessarily the corresponding component of the [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), and excludes gradient-driven diffusive flux, residual stress, and momentum sources.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection transports vertical momentum along the chosen positive normal of the transport surface.

items.name: effective_electron_diffusivity
items.description: Directional electron particle diffusion coefficient linking a direction-specific effective diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Effective electron diffusivity is an effective scalar transport coefficient for diffusive electron-particle transport along a specified transport direction in a magnetized plasma. It is the direction-specific coefficient appearing in a macroscopic particle-transport closure for electrons.

The directional constitutive relation is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{eff}}\,\nabla_\alpha n_e
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the specified oriented transport direction, $\Gamma_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the component of the diffusive electron particle-flux vector along that direction, $D_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective electron diffusivity for the same direction, $\nabla_\alpha n_e$ is the component of the gradient of electron number density along $\alpha$, and $n_e$ is electron number density. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusive transport when $D_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is positive.

This quantity applies to electron particles in the magnetized plasma and has no isotope or charge-state aggregation. It describes the diffusive contribution only and excludes convective particle fluxes, particle sources, and sinks; the qualifier effective identifies a reduced coefficient for the represented diffusive flux component, not a microscopic collision-only diffusion coefficient or a species-independent particle diffusivity.

This is the effective branch of electron diffusivity. The directional specialization [radial effective electron diffusivity](name:radial_effective_electron_diffusivity) is the specialization for the $\hat R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: coolant_volume_of_breeder_blanket
items.description: Total geometric volume occupied by lead-lithium coolant/breeder throughout the breeder blanket assembly, excluding external coolant loops and other blanket materials.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the total volume occupied by the lead-lithium coolant/breeder constituent within the complete breeder blanket assembly. It is a material-specific component of the broader volume of breeder blanket and is distinct from the volume of an individual module or layer.

$$
V_{\mathrm{PbLi}} = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{blanket}}} \chi_{\mathrm{PbLi}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{PbLi}}$ is the PbLi volume, $\Omega_{\mathrm{blanket}}$ is the volume of the complete breeder blanket assembly, $\chi_{\mathrm{PbLi}}$ is one inside the PbLi region and zero elsewhere, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is an elemental volume. The integral excludes external coolant loops, structural materials, voids, and other non-PbLi constituents.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
items.description: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of magnetic-field-aligned ordered flow momentum carried by ions of one specified species and charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of the magnetic-field-aligned component of ordered [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified species and charge state. The parallel direction follows the local magnetic field, rather than a fixed geometric axis.

In a linear damping contribution to the momentum balance, the rate multiplies the selected parallel momentum density as follows:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial g_{s,\parallel}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\parallel} g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $g_{s,\parallel}$ is the ordered momentum density of the selected ion species and charge state along the magnetic field, $s$ identifies that species and charge state, $t$ is time, and $\nu_{s,\parallel}$ is this damping rate. The subscript $\parallel$ denotes projection along the local magnetic field, and $\mathrm{damp}$ restricts the derivative to the damping contribution. For a constant positive rate, this term alone produces exponential relaxation with a time scale equal to the reciprocal of the rate; a zero rate means this damping contribution is absent. A nonnegative rate damps either sign of the selected momentum component.

The coefficient applies to one ion species and one charge state, without summation or averaging over species or charge states. It describes local relaxation, not diffusive or convective momentum transport or an additive momentum source. Collisional relaxation of this population can transfer momentum to other populations and therefore does not by itself imply loss of total plasma momentum.

This is the parallel component of the [ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) and a specialization of the broader [momentum damping rate](name:momentum_damping_rate). The aggregate [parallel ion momentum damping rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate) is distinct; its charge-state aggregation is a density-weighted mean over all charge states, not a sum. The [poloidal](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), [radial](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), and [toroidal](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) charge-state rates select other directional components. In particular, the radial component is along $\hat R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height; the basis satisfies $\hat R \times \hat\phi = \hat Z$.

items.name: neutral_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective particle diffusivity relating a neutral species’ internal-state-summed diffusive flux to its opposing number-density gradient, without selecting a spatial direction.
items.documentation:
The neutral diffusion coefficient characterizes local Fickian particle diffusion of a specified neutral species without selecting a spatial direction. It describes the aggregate neutral population rather than particles in one specified internal state.

For a scalar Fickian closure, the diffusive particle flux satisfies:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0,\mathrm{diff}} = -D^0\nabla n_0
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the neutral diffusive particle flux density, $D^0$ is the neutral diffusion coefficient, $n_0$ is the neutral number density, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.
