The label $0$ denotes neutral particles. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for nonnegative diffusivity.

The number density and diffusive particle flux are summed over all internal states of the specified neutral species, not over different neutral species. This distinguishes the quantity from the [neutral-state diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_state_diffusion_coefficient), which applies to a specified internal state. It excludes convective particle transport and is distinct from energy and momentum diffusion coefficients.

The [radial neutral diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient) specializes the same particle-diffusion response to the major-radius direction; no directional component is selected here.

items.name: neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description: Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of a multicomponent plasma, equal to total momentum density divided by total mass density.
items.documentation:
Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of a multicomponent plasma. It is the velocity whose product with total mass density equals the total momentum density of the included species.

The center-of-mass velocity $\mathbf{V}_{cm}$ is defined as

$$
\mathbf{V}_{cm} = \frac{\sum_s m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\sum_s m_s n_s} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\rho}
$$

where $s$ indexes the included species, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $n_s$ is the number density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the species fluid velocity, $\rho_s=m_s n_s$ is the species mass density, and $\rho=\sum_s\rho_s$ is the total mass density.

The weighting is by mass density, not charge, number density alone, or an unweighted species average. Directional projections retain this definition; for example, [vertical neutral-species center-of-mass velocity](name:vertical_neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity) applies the same barycentric weighting to the neutral-species contribution. This quantity is the common vector context for [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) component forms.

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component is directed along the positive basis vector of its explicitly specified coordinate system; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, these directions are $+\hat{R}$ toward increasing major radius, $+\hat{\phi}$ toward increasing toroidal angle, and $+\hat{Z}$ upward.

items.name: thickness_of_cryostat
items.description: Local through-wall distance across the cryostat structural vessel, measured along the wall normal between its inner and outer material faces.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the geometric thickness of the cryostat structural vessel at a specified location. It is the separation through the wall material between corresponding inner and outer faces, measured along the local wall-normal direction.

At the corresponding inner and outer face points, the thickness is defined by

$$
t = (\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{out}}-\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{in}})\mathbin{\cdot}\hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $t$ is the thickness in m, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{out}}$ are the face position vectors in m, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the inner face toward the outer face.

The value is a non-negative material separation and excludes gaps, insulation, and attached components. It is distinct from [thickness of the vacuum vessel](name:thickness_of_vacuum_vessel), which describes the vacuum-vessel wall rather than the cryostat structural wall.

items.name: fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Local net Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate per unit volume into a nonthermal fast-particle population, including all guiding-center orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle collisional power density is the local net rate at which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic-energy density of a specified nonthermal particle population. It includes all guiding-center orbit classes and is a collisional source or sink, not stored kinetic-energy density.

It is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a\in\mathrm{fast}} \sum_b \int E_a(\mathbf{v})\,C_{ab}[f_a,f_b](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-particle collisional power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $a$ indexes fast species in the target population, $b$ indexes charged collision partners, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $E_a$ is the kinetic energy of one particle of species $a$. The functions $f_a$ and $f_b$ are the respective phase-space number distributions, $C_{ab}$ gives the collisional time derivative of $f_a$ due to partner $b$, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration measure.

The target population is not restricted to fast electrons or to a single ion species. Contributions from its constituent distributions are added. The partner sum includes the charged partners represented in the specified collisional contribution; electron-to-fast-particle exchange is the contribution with electrons as the collision partner. This quantity is local, not a flux-surface average or volume-integrated power.

The [co-passing contribution](name:co_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing contribution](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions), together with the trapped contribution, sum to this orbit-unrestricted quantity when these classes exhaust the fast-particle population.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic-energy density of the fast-particle population; negative when they decrease it.

items.name: total_ion_energy_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective transport velocity that multiplies the summed energy density of all ion species to give their combined convective energy flux.
items.documentation:
Total ion energy convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient relating the combined convective energy flux of all ion species to their summed local transported energy density. It is the all-ion aggregate of [ion energy convection velocity](name:ion_energy_convection_velocity).

The defining energy-flux relation is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = W_i^{\mathrm{tot}}\,\mathbf{v}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the summed convective ion-energy flux, $W_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the summed local transported ion-energy density, and $\mathbf{v}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion energy convection velocity. The subscript $i$ denotes ions, and the superscript $\mathrm{tot}$ denotes aggregation over all ion species.

The energy density and convective flux include all ion species and their ionic charge states; electron and neutral contributions are excluded. When species convection velocities use the same energy-flux definition, the aggregate coefficient is their energy-density-weighted mean, not their arithmetic sum. It is an effective transport coefficient, not necessarily the ion bulk-flow velocity, and excludes the gradient-driven diffusive contribution to energy flux.

This quantity specializes the population-independent [energy convection velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity) to the combined ion energy channel without restricting the transport direction or plasma region. Its [parallel component](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity) is the projection along the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the corresponding projected total ion convective energy flux points along the positive direction of that projection.

items.name: radial_neutral_velocity
items.description: Signed major-radius component of a neutral species' mean flow in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, with number-density-weighted averaging over contributing internal states.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral velocity is the major-radius projection of the mean translational flow of a selected neutral species in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It represents directed neutral motion after averaging over particle velocities and over the contributing internal states.

The component and its internal-state averaging are defined by:

$$
u_{0R}=\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{u}_0=\frac{\sum_a n_{0,a}\,\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{u}_{0,a}}{\sum_a n_{0,a}}
$$

where $u_{0R}$ is the radial neutral velocity, $\mathbf{u}_0$ is the mean [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity), $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius, $a$ indexes the included neutral internal states, $n_{0,a}$ is their number density, and $\mathbf{u}_{0,a}$ is their mean particle velocity. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The averaging combines internal states of the selected neutral species, not different species or ionized charge states. Velocities are density-weighted means, not sums. This quantity is a directional component, not the flow speed, thermal velocity spread, particle flux, or projection normal to a magnetic flux surface.

The [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) retains one state's vector flow rather than averaging over contributing states. The [toroidal neutral velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_velocity) is the toroidal projection of the same state-averaged neutral flow.

Sign convention: Positive when the mean neutral flow points toward increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to trapped fast electrons, obtained by applying the major-radius lever arm to the toroidal collisional force density.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum transfer density delivered by Coulomb collisions to the trapped-orbit part of the fast-electron population. It is the toroidal component of trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions, resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional torque density, $R$ is the major radius, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal component of the collisional force density acting on trapped fast electrons. The quantity excludes torque transferred to other electron orbit classes or particle species.

Its population scope distinguishes it from [toroidal_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons), which includes the full fast-electron population.

Sign convention: Positive when the collisional torque acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, increasing the trapped fast-electron toroidal angular momentum.

items.name: thermal_ion_pressure
items.description: Pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress from random motion, summed over ionic charge states and excluding fast-ion pressure and bulk-flow stress.
items.documentation:
Pressure of thermal ions is the isotropic kinetic stress associated with random thermal motion. It equals one-third of the trace of the thermal pressure tensor, whose velocity moments are taken relative to the thermal population's mean flow.

For an ion species, the thermal pressure is the additive sum of its charge-state contributions:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \sum_c p_{i,c,\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal pressure of ion species $i$, $c$ labels its ionic charge states, and $p_{i,c,\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal pressure of an individual ion charge state](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_pressure). The subscript $\mathrm{th}$ denotes the thermal population.

The species-resolved quantity includes all ionic charge states of that species. The [total thermal ion pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure) additionally sums these contributions over all ion species. Both aggregations are direct pressure sums, not density-weighted means.

This quantity is the thermal contribution to [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure); it excludes nonthermal fast-ion pressure, directed bulk-flow stress, electron pressure, and neutral pressure. The all-species thermal-ion contribution combines with thermal-electron pressure to form [thermal plasma pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure).

items.name: poloidal_beta
items.description: Poloidal beta compares volume-averaged total perpendicular plasma pressure with an effective poloidal magnetic-pressure scale set by net plasma current and plasma geometry.
items.documentation:
Poloidal beta compares the total perpendicular plasma pressure, averaged over the whole plasma volume, with a magnetic-pressure scale associated with the poloidal field. The reference scale is defined by the net plasma current and plasma geometry.

The defining pressure ratio and its current-based normalization are

$$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$

Here $\beta_\mathrm{p}$ is poloidal beta; $p$ is the [total perpendicular plasma pressure](name:perpendicular_plasma_pressure); $V$ is the whole plasma volume; $dV$ is a volume element; and $\langle p\rangle=V^{-1}\int_V p\,dV$ is the volume-averaged pressure. The symbols $R_0$, $\mu_0$, and $I_\mathrm{p}$ denote the reference major radius, vacuum permeability, and net toroidal plasma current, respectively. The effective reference poloidal-field magnitude $B_{\mathrm{p,ref}}$ is fixed by $B_{\mathrm{p,ref}}^2=\mu_0^2 I_\mathrm{p}^2V/(2R_0)$.

The pressure includes electron and ion contributions from both thermal and nonthermal populations. This is a whole-plasma quantity, not an electron-only or point-local beta, and it is not the volume average of local pressure-to-magnetic-pressure ratios. The reference poloidal field is a current-based scale rather than a local field magnitude. The normalization requires nonzero net plasma current.

Unlike [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta), which uses a reference toroidal field, poloidal beta uses the poloidal magnetic-pressure scale. For the same volume-averaged pressure and a combined magnetic-pressure scale equal to the sum of the component scales, [total beta](name:beta) satisfies $1/\beta=1/\beta_\mathrm{p}+1/\beta_\mathrm{t}$, where $\beta$ is total beta and $\beta_\mathrm{t}$ is toroidal beta.

items.name: parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
items.description: Effective kinematic coefficient relating the diffusive flux of field-parallel edge-plasma bulk momentum to the opposing flow-velocity gradient along the magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Parallel edge-plasma momentum diffusivity is the effective kinematic coefficient governing diffusion of field-parallel bulk [momentum](name:momentum) along the magnetic field in the plasma edge. It is the field-aligned specialization of [edge-plasma momentum diffusivity](name:edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity).

In a local down-gradient closure, the field-parallel diffusive flux of parallel momentum is:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\rho_m \chi_{\parallel}\,\hat{b}\cdot\nabla u_{\parallel}
$$

where $\Pi_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux of parallel bulk momentum along the magnetic field, $\rho_m$ is the aggregate plasma mass density, $\chi_{\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $u_{\parallel}$ is the projection of the mass-density-weighted bulk plasma velocity onto that direction, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The coefficient applies to aggregate edge-plasma momentum, rather than momentum of a single ion species or charge state; neutral-population momentum is excluded. The closure uses total plasma mass density and mass-density-weighted bulk flow, not a sum of species diffusivities. It acts on the field-parallel velocity gradient, rather than the gradient of momentum density.

This coefficient describes gradient-driven diffusion, distinct from the advective transport parameterized by [parallel momentum convection velocity](name:parallel_momentum_convection_velocity). Convective transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources are excluded from the diffusive contribution.

items.name: current_density_due_to_fast_ion
items.description: Vector density of electric current carried by a specified charged-particle contribution, obtained from its signed charge-weighted particle flux.
items.documentation:
A current-density contribution is the local electric current carried by the charged particles included in the specified population or contribution. It is a vector whose components are charge-weighted particle fluxes, not a particle or energy density.

$$
\mathbf{J} = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species or population $s$, $f_s$ is its velocity-distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $t$ is time. The sum and velocity-space domain include only the explicitly specified contributing populations. Component and population specializations retain this definition; for example, [toroidal current density due to fast ions](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_fast_ion) excludes the compensating electron back current.

Sign convention: Positive when a reported current-density component points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

items.name: ion_atomic_mass
items.description: Ion atomic mass is the neutral-atom reference mass of a selected elemental or isotopic constituent of an ion species, including bound electrons and independent of ionic charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion atomic mass is the reference mass assigned to one neutral atom of a selected elemental or isotopic constituent of an ion species. It specifies atomic composition and includes the bound-electron contribution of the neutral reference atom.

The atomic mass is related to the corresponding relative atomic mass by

$$
m_i = A_{\mathrm r,i}\,m_{\mathrm u}
$$

where $i$ labels the ion species, $m_i$ is the selected constituent's reference atomic mass, $A_{\mathrm r,i}$ is its relative atomic mass, and $m_{\mathrm u}$ is the atomic mass constant, defined as one twelfth of the rest mass of a free neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground state.

The value applies per constituent atom, not to the total ion population or, for a molecular ion, to the entire molecule. It is independent of ionic charge state and is not the charge-dependent rest mass of an actual ion, the integer nucleon count called the mass number, a mass density, or a mass flow rate.

This quantity specializes [atomic mass](name:atomic_mass) to constituents of ion species without restricting them to thermal or nonthermal populations. [Fast-ion atomic mass](name:fast_ion_atomic_mass) is the corresponding specialization for a nonthermal ion species.

items.name: length_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Euclidean length of an inclined side of an oblique parallelogram cross-section of a magnetic component, defining one of its oblique geometric dimensions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the Euclidean length of a designated inclined side of an oblique parallelogram cross-section of a magnetic component. It defines one oblique geometric dimension independently of the component's particular identity or side-label convention.

The edge length is defined in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame by

$$
L = \sqrt{(R_2-R_1)^2 + (Z_2-Z_1)^2}
$$

where $L$ is the edge length, $R_1$ and $R_2$ are the major-radius coordinates of the endpoints, and $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ are their vertical-height coordinates; all length coordinates are in meters. The endpoints share the same toroidal angle $\phi$.

The selected edge may be distinguished by its inclination or geometric role. [major_length_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:major_length_of_poloidal_field_coil) is a concrete poloidal-field-coil instance, while length_of_passive_structure and [major_length_of_iron_core_segment](name:major_length_of_iron_core_segment) apply the same geometric concept to other magnetic components. This quantity is distinct from a cross-sectional height, width, or area.

items.name: extent_of_detector_pixel
items.description: Extent of a detector pixel is the nonnegative linear size of one pixel footprint along either the first or second local tangential axis in the right-handed local detector frame (first local tangential, second local tangential, detector normal). It excludes optical resolution and spacing or inactive gaps between neighboring pixels.
items.documentation:
Extent of a detector pixel is the nonnegative linear size of one pixel footprint along a specified in-plane axis of the right-handed local detector frame $(\hat{t}_1,\hat{t}_2,\hat{n})$, where $\hat{t}_1$ and $\hat{t}_2$ are the first and second local tangential directions in the detector plane and $\hat{n}$ is the detector-plane normal. The footprint is the area assigned to that pixel for geometric mapping or active collection, independent of the optical point-spread function.

For a coordinate $s_a$ along the selected local tangential axis, the extent is the separation of the footprint boundaries:

$$
r_a = s_{a,+} - s_{a,-}
$$

where $a$ is either $1$ or $2$ and selects the axis $\hat{t}_a$, $r_a$ is the detector-pixel extent in meters, $s_{a,-}$ and $s_{a,+}$ are the lower and upper footprint-boundary coordinates in meters along $\hat{t}_a$, and $s_{a,+} \ge s_{a,-}$. Consequently $r_a \ge 0$.

This quantity is a footprint-edge separation, not the detector-pixel center location, the center-to-center pitch, the optical point-spread width, or the spacing or inactive gap between neighboring pixels. The detector-pixel center location is described by separate coordinate quantities, such as horizontal coordinate of detector pixel and [vertical coordinate of detector pixel](name:vertical_coordinate_of_detector_pixel). The extent equals the pitch along the same selected axis only when adjacent pixel footprints tile the detector plane contiguously with negligible inactive gap; this condition is independent of whether the footprint is square or non-square.

items.name: fast_particle_energy
items.description: Fast-particle energy is the total kinetic energy stored in a specified suprathermal population, integrated over the plasma volume and including motion parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle energy is the total kinetic energy carried by a specified suprathermal population throughout the plasma volume. It includes motion both parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field, without restriction to a particular species or heating mechanism.

The defining kinetic-energy moment is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{fast}}(t)=\sum_s\int_V d^3x\int d^3p\,\mathcal{E}_{s,\mathrm{kin}}(\mathbf{p})\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{p},t)
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle energy, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes the included particle species, $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{p}$ is particle momentum, $\mathcal{E}_{s,\mathrm{kin}}$ is the single-particle kinetic energy excluding rest energy, and $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle number distribution per physical-volume and momentum-space element.

The integral includes only the specified fast population, not thermal particles that may coexist in the full distribution. Contributions from included species and charge states are summed as energies, not averaged. This is the global fast-population energy-moment specialization of [particle energy](name:particle_energy), rather than a single-particle energy coordinate.

The [parallel fast-particle energy](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) characterizes field-aligned motion using three-halves of the parallel-pressure integral, whereas the [perpendicular fast-particle energy](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) describes energy associated with perpendicular motion. The parallel quantity's pressure-based normalization must be distinguished from an unscaled parallel kinetic-energy contribution when relating these directional quantities to the total.

items.name: radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Radial diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of momentum in the aggregate neutral population, summed over all resolved neutral internal states.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral momentum diffusion coefficient is the effective coefficient for diffusive transport of neutral-particle momentum in the radial direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is the radial component of the momentum-diffusion tensor represented by the [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).

The radial diffusive neutral momentum flux density is governed by:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{diff},R} = -\rho_n D_{\mathrm{mom},R} \frac{\partial u_{n,R}}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{diff},R}$ is the radial component of the neutral momentum diffusive flux density, $\rho_n$ is the mass density of the aggregate neutral population, $D_{\mathrm{mom},R}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $u_{n,R}$ is the radial component of the aggregate neutral flow velocity, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate. The negative sign indicates that diffusive transport opposes the radial gradient of radial neutral flow velocity.

This quantity applies to the aggregate neutral population, with contributions combined over all resolved neutral internal states. It represents transport along the cylindrical radial direction of increasing $R$, not the parallel component along magnetic-field lines or a coefficient for an individual neutral internal state. It is a diffusion coefficient rather than a momentum flux or a convective velocity.

As the radial component of the parent tensor, it supplies the radial entry of the [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient); the corresponding field-aligned entry is the [parallel neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: ion_absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to ion populations, integrated over the plasma volume and partitioned into thermal and fast-ion contributions.
items.documentation:
Ion absorbed wave power is the total rate of energy transfer from coherent electromagnetic waves to ion populations. It includes direct absorption by both bulk thermal ions and suprathermal fast ions.

The volume-integrated ion power is defined by

$$
P_i^{\mathrm{abs}} = \int_V p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{abs}} + P_{i,\mathrm{thermal}}^{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_i^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total ion absorbed wave power, $p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local wave power deposition density to ions, $V$ is the plasma volume, and the two terms are the [fast-ion absorbed wave power](name:fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [thermal-ion absorbed wave power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power). This quantity is the ion component of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), excluding power transferred directly to electron populations; [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power) represents the corresponding electron channel.

items.name: ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive energy flux carried by ions to their local temperature gradient, without selecting a transport direction.
items.documentation:
The effective ion energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven energy transport carried by a specified ion population. It is the ion-specific specialization of the [energy diffusion coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient).

For a single-temperature scalar Fickian closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_i} = -D_{i,W}\,\nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux density, $n_i$ is the number density of the included ions, $D_{i,W}$ is their effective energy diffusion coefficient, and $T_i$ is their energy-valued temperature. The subscript $i$ identifies ions, $W$ identifies the energy channel, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. For positive diffusivity, the minus sign gives transport down the temperature gradient.

At species scope, the coefficient is a density-weighted mean over all charge states, not a sum of charge-state coefficients. For a collective ion population, this mean extends over all included ion species and charge states. This averaging preserves the displayed flux relation when the constituent populations share the temperature gradient. The [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead resolves one specified charge state.

The quantity selects neither a spatial region nor a transport direction; this does not require isotropic transport. The [parallel specialization](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) selects transport along the magnetic field. The [thermal-ion specialization](name:thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) restricts the carrier population, while the [total-ion specialization](name:total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) specifies total ion-energy aggregation.

Convective and advective energy fluxes are excluded from the diffusive contribution. The coefficient is distinct from particle diffusion and from thermal conductivity, which relates heat flux directly to a temperature gradient without density normalization.

items.name: fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Fast electron power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Fast electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power transferred to the fast, non-thermal electron population throughout the plasma volume. It is the fast-electron component of [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power).

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron absorbed wave power, $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local coherent-wave power density absorbed by fast electrons at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity excludes wave power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons, ions, and other populations, as well as wave power that is launched but not absorbed. Unlike [fast electron power at inside flux surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it represents the total plasma-volume integral rather than a cumulative value inside a specified flux surface. The population scope is complementary to [thermal electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective advective velocity vector relating the number density of a neutral species in a specified internal state to its convective particle flux in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state particle convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of the density-proportional advective particle flux for a specified internal state of a neutral species in the edge plasma. It describes directed transport after density-gradient-driven diffusion has been separated.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_{n,a}\mathbf{v}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ labels the selected internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is that state's convective neutral-particle flux, $n_{n,a}$ is its neutral-particle number density, and $\mathbf{v}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection velocity.

The population includes thermal and nonthermal particles of the selected neutral state; no sum or average over internal states or species is implied. The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport, describes particle transport rather than heat or momentum transport, and need not equal the bulk neutral-flow velocity. Unlike [ion-charge-state particle convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity), it resolves neutral internal states rather than ionic charge states.

No directional projection is imposed on this vector. The [poloidal neutral-state particle convection velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity) is its poloidal projection, while the [parallel neutral-state particle convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity) is its projection along the magnetic-field direction. Both retain the same neutral-state population and particle-transport scope.
